Sibling fields can drift silently because no test fails. The 2026-05-14 GEO canonical-to-root decision also retroactively narrowed S138's just-shipped /en/ self-canonical posture within 24 hours — the verifier needed extension *before* shipping the original /en/ emission, not after a strategic re-decision surfaced the gap. | When introducing locale/state-aware emission for any metadata field, extend the parity verifier to assert **every sibling field in the same OG/Schema block** before shipping, not after. For S139: extended `tests/build/og-url-canonical-parity.test.ts` to assert `og:locale` primary parity + `og:locale:alternate` symmetric-absence + canonical-to-root across 13 hub pairs + 1 event pair. Sibling-Field Drift Detection pattern banked in `patterns.md`. (S139, 2026-05-14) |
| **Content-page.ts canonical never matched its locale** (surfaced during S139 SSR verification, 2026-05-14). Session A's Explore probe reported "`content-page.ts` already emits root URL regardless of locale" — partially true. `content-page.ts:61` emits `${BASE_URL}/${slug}/`; the caller at `src/generate-site.ts:715` passes `slug: 'en/about'` for /en/ content pages. The result: `/en/about/index.html` canonical was `https://agentathens.com/en/about/` (self-canonical, NOT root). Same for og:url. The bug was invisible to the parity verifier because content pages weren't in its coverage at the time. | The Explore agent's "no urlPrefix in content-page.ts" statement was technically true but missed that the locale prefix was baked into the `slug` parameter upstream. Probing the template alone can miss caller-side composition. The verifier's per-template scope (hubs + events) created the blind spot. | Two structural improvements: (a) `content-page.ts` now derives `rootSlug = slug.replace(/^en\//, '')` and uses it for canonical/og:url (S139 fix); (b) extend the parity verifier to cover content pages (banked as follow-up — not in S139 to limit scope). When probing emission, also probe callers — the field value lives in the composition, not just the template. (S139, 2026-05-14) |
| **Netlify CLI deploy can report exit 0 while deploy state=error** (2026-05-14, S139 post-deploy). `netlify deploy --prod --dir=dist` returned exit code 0 after CLI logged "Uploading 0 files" + "Deploy is live!" — but the platform-side state for that deploy ID was `error` with `error_message: "Deploy canceled"`. Production continued serving the prior successful deploy. The CLI returns success on **upload completion**, not on platform-side acceptance. No concurrent deploy was visible in the API to explain the cancellation; the site's `build_settings.stop_builds: true` rules out git-push-auto-deploy as the canceler. Root cause for this specific cancellation is **open** — most likely transient Netlify platform issue, possibly a parallel CLI deploy attempt that didn't surface its own record. The S138 deploy's "Uploading 0 files" message was the same symptom (Netlify deduped to a deploy that was probably already canceled or queued) — but went undetected because production happened to still serve correct content via a successful deploy from earlier in the chain. **Detectability of silent rollback depends on whether the change is structurally visible in live HTML** — subtle visual or metadata-only changes can mask canceled deploys for long periods. S139's canonical-to-root flip was structurally visible (curl can spot it), so the silent rollback surfaced fast; S138's Option 2 shape-based saved-state was subtle enough that "still serving working old version" wouldn't have triggered any alarm. This bug class has likely been silently present across prior cycles whenever the live diff wasn't load-bearing for `curl` or other lightweight probes. | CLI exit 0 ≠ deploy success. The CLI surfaces transport-layer success ("the bytes reached Netlify"), not platform-layer success ("the deploy was accepted, built, and published"). A canceled or errored deploy produces no CLI failure, no stderr output, and no non-zero exit code — the failure is only visible via the platform API or by hitting the production URL and observing stale content. Silent rollback is the failure mode: production keeps serving the prior deploy, looking fine to anyone not specifically checking against expected new output. | **Always verify deploy state via API after `netlify deploy --prod`.** Concretely: `netlify api getSiteDeploy --data '{"site_id": "<id>", "deploy_id": "<id-from-CLI-output>"}'` and confirm `state: "ready"`. The CLI prints the unique deploy URL on completion — extract the deploy_id from that URL (`https://<deploy-id>--<site>.netlify.app`). If `state != "ready"`, the deploy did not publish; production is serving the prior version. Secondary verification: `curl -sI <prod-url>` to check `etag` / `age` headers, and `curl -s <prod-url> | grep <recently-changed-string>` to confirm the new content is live. Adjunct: if a deploy shows `state: "error"` with `error_message: "Deploy canceled"` and no concurrent deploy is visible in `listSiteDeploys`, re-run the deploy — most cancellation causes are transient. (S139, 2026-05-14) |

(S140, 2026-05-14.) |

Pavlopoulos on megaron.gr listing: "Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη και απονομή Δικαιοσύνης – Προκόπης Παυλόπουλος." Same URL, same date, different title → `generateEventId` at scrape-megaron.ts:28-31 hashed `${title}-${startDate}` and produced a different ID. `upsertEvent` performed an INSERT (not UPDATE) for the "new" event. Result: two Pavlopoulos rows scheduled for 2026-05-29, one `concert`, one `other`. | `generateEventId(title, startDate)` is the dedup key. Title changes between scrapes are not anticipated — but megaron.gr's listing-page title sometimes differs from its event-detail-page title (which is what was originally scraped via newsletter or earlier listing). The scraper has no awareness that the same URL it's hitting has already produced a row under a different generated ID. | Subsequent dedup pass via `scripts/remove-duplicates.ts` caught the URL-equality but its "keep highest quality" logic biased toward the older row (longer description, longer-in-DB), undoing the type fix. **Two follow-up options to consider in a maintenance batch:** (a) change `generateEventId` to hash on `url + start_date` instead of `title + start_date` — URL is the stable identity, title can change as the source updates copy; would have made the upsert a true UPDATE and avoided the dedup detour entirely; (b) add a `--prefer-newest` flag to `remove-duplicates.ts` for cases where newer rows have intentionally-better metadata. Resolved this session via 5 targeted manual UPDATEs (user-approved) — fine for one demo, but the underlying ID-stability question is real. (S140, 2026-05-14.) |



## 2026-05-17 — Bing API Integration + Visibility CSV Schema Lock (revised S136, GSC half deferred to S138)

| What went wrong | Why | Correct approach |
|---|---|---|
| **Pre-session brief assumed Bing API key was populated; reality was a 0-byte file at the canonical path.** Step 0a's expected `BLOCKED: Bing API key absent` failure mode doesn't fire for an empty file — `[ -f "$KEY" ]` passes happily on a 0-byte placeholder. Without hardening, the spike would have hit the Bing API with an empty `apikey=` query parameter, gotten back a 401, and the fetcher would have written `status='auth_fail'` — which the operator would have read as "GSC silent-fail strikes again, key revoked," prompting a re-issue cycle. Real cause: key not yet pasted into the pre-staged file. | Bare presence checks on credential files don't distinguish "operator created the file with `touch && chmod 600` to pre-stage" from "operator pasted the key in." Both produce a file. Only `[ -s file ]` (size > 0) distinguishes the two states. | Step 0a was hardened to `[ -s "$KEY" ]` during Phase 1 verification — the empty-file state surfaces as a distinct BLOCKED variant ("Bing key file exists but is empty (0 bytes)"). Pattern banked in `patterns.md` as a sub-case of "verify-assumptions" — for any pre-staged credential file, check non-empty contents, not just presence. |
| **Bing Webmaster API response shape gotchas (three of them) discovered during Step 1 spike.** (1) The response is wrapped in `{d: [...]}` for some endpoints and `{d: {results: [...]}}` for others — WCF JSON serialization legacy. (2) The `Date` field is `/Date(1778223600000-0700)/` — .NET epoch-milliseconds-with-timezone-offset, requires a custom parser. (3) `GetPageStats` reuses the `QueryStats` `__type` and puts the page URL in the `Query` field — counter-intuitive but documented this way. Without the spike, the production fetcher would have unwrapped the wrong shape and parsed dates as ISO strings, returning empty or wrong aggregates that silently passed tests. | Bing's API predates modern JSON conventions; it's a SOAP-over-JSON facade. The `__type` field hints at the actual record type, but the field NAMES on the response don't always match the endpoint name (GetPageStats returns rows shaped like QueryStats). Trusting endpoint naming as a guide to response shape produces wrong assumptions. | Always run a 5-min spike that prints raw response (first 500 chars) + parsed keys before writing production fetch code. The spike at `scripts/bing-spike.ts` was deleted after green; its output remains in the session transcript. Pattern: when integrating any unfamiliar API, the spike's diagnostic value is the raw-response print, not the green-checks; even when all checks pass, the raw print reveals the shape choices needed for the production fetcher. |
| **The plan referenced `--dry-run` on the monitor; the monitor doesn't have that flag.** Plan's Step 4 verify said `bun run scripts/monitor-search-visibility.ts --dry-run`. Reality: monitor's argv parsing only knows `--update`, `--force`, and the manual-metrics flags. Running without `--dry-run` appends a real row. | Brief carried "dry-run is a universal flag" assumption forward; not all scripts in this codebase implement it. Sympathy-update would be adding `--dry-run` to the monitor, but that's scope creep for verification convenience alone. | Ran the monitor live, inspected the appended row (27 cols, GSC=STALE × 4, Bing=0 × 4 from logs/bing-latest.json). The row IS the verification; no dry-run is needed when the data file is structured enough to inspect post-hoc. Plan-side note: don't assume `--dry-run` exists on every CLI; check `process.argv.includes(...)` calls before referencing the flag in verify steps. |
| **`data/search-visibility-log.csv` is gitignored** but the plan's Step 7 commit list included it. Pre-existing infrastructure choice (CSV is operational state, not source). Brief's commit list was generated from "files modified by the session" without checking gitignore status. | When the plan lists files to commit, it conflates "files this session changed" with "files git will track." Gitignored files appear in `git status` (as untracked or modified-but-ignored) but won't appear in `git diff --cached` after `git add`. Without the explicit gitignore check, the commit appears successful but the file isn't actually staged. | `git add` on gitignored files silently no-ops (no error). `git diff --cached --stat` reveals what's actually staged. Always reconcile commit-list against `git ls-files <path>` (tracked?) and `git check-ignore -v <path>` (ignored?) before staging. Two prior sessions hit related issues with `data/` gitignore patterns (S91, S97). This is now [[feedback_stage_precisely]] instance #4. |
| **The `com.agentathens.monitor-visibility.plist` lives only in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, not in the repo.** Other plists are versioned at the project root (`com.agentathens.daily.plist`, `com.agentathens.enrichment-check.plist`), so the missing one stood out only when checking source-of-truth for the Step 5 edit. The session edit to chain `fetch-bing-metrics.ts` before the monitor is therefore not under version control. | Pre-existing infrastructure gap — the visibility plist was created externally during S91/S100 prep and never copied to the repo. The repo's other plists set a precedent that any new plist edit "must" be versioned, but this one isn't. Editing in place was the pragmatic choice; the gap remains. | Flagged as a follow-up: copy `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agentathens.monitor-visibility.plist` to the project root for versioning. Not done in this session (out of S136 scope; would add a 12th file to the commit). When this gap is closed, the chained `fetch-bing-metrics.ts; monitor-search-visibility.ts` becomes auditable in git history. |

(b) Column name: brief said `ai_citations`; reality is `ai_citations_count`. (c) Column count math: brief said 28 cols; reality is 27 (20 − 1 + 8). | Memory crystallization continues to be the dominant failure mode at brief-write time. Each mistake-class is small (a string, a number, a path); each catch is cheap (a single grep or `head -1`); the cumulative cost of NOT catching them is much larger because each propagates through every downstream step until the first verification surface. | Phase 1 verification with parallel Explore agents (1-3) before plan finalization remains the highest-leverage mitigation. ## S142 — Stale agentathens.com / Netlify deploy verification + --no-build (2026-05-18)

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| **`netlify deploy --prod --dir=dist` runs the configured site build command (`bun run build` per `build_settings.cmd`) before deploying, unless `--no-build` is passed.** This was the actual recurring "Netlify CLI deploy failed" since 2026-04-10 (43 stderr entries documented in `logs/freshness-stderr.log`), not the silent-rollback gotcha banked May 14. The CLI's pre-deploy build step fails under launchd's environment (different PATH/working-dir semantics from an interactive shell), aborts with exit non-zero, and stderr reads `Error: Error while running build`. Earlier-month deploys that succeeded happened to hit the CLI under interactive-shell state where `bun run build` worked. The script at `scripts/daily-automated.sh:536` (pre-fix) had no `--no-build` flag — every launchd-driven deploy was a coin-flip on environment state. | The CLI flag set `--prod --dir=dist` is *not* equivalent to "deploy this prebuilt directory and skip building." The CLI still reads the site's build configuration and attempts to run the configured command before deploying, *as if it were doing CI*. When dist/ is already built by an upstream step (the pipeline's PHASE: SITE GENERATION), the redundant build is at best wasteful and at worst environment-dependent failure. Confirmed via `netlify deploy --help` showing `--no-build` flag description: "Do not run build command before deploying. Only use this if you …". | Always pass `--no-build` when deploying a prebuilt artifact. The deploy-script invariant: if `dist/` exists at deploy time, `--no-build` is mandatory. Fixed at `scripts/daily-automated.sh:559` (S142 commit `c9ae3b53f`). Cross-reference: this is the *applied* version of the May-14 gotcha note (mistakes.md:622+) which described the *silent* failure mode; this entry describes the *loud* failure mode (CLI exit non-zero) that's been recurring since 2026-04-10. Both fixes ship in the same deploy_to_netlify rewrite. |
| **`netlify api` JSON responses embed ASCII control characters in description fields, causing strict `jq` to abort with `parse error: Invalid string: control characters from U+0000 through U+001F must be escaped`.** The `getSiteDeploy` response includes a `deploy_validations_report` block with `description` strings containing literal U+001F separators (or similar low-ASCII bytes) at line ~109 column 1 in the formatted output. `jq` defaults to strict JSON parsing and refuses these strings; `python3 -c 'json.loads(...)'` accepts the same payload silently. Without the strip, every state-poll iteration in the new deploy_to_netlify() failed parsing and the loop spun on `state=` (empty). Surfaced during S142 implementation; recovered with `tr -d`. | The Netlify API gateway/serializer doesn't escape U+0000–U+001F bytes embedded in user-supplied description strings (validation rule output, presumably). The bytes pass through the API response intact. jq's strict mode is correct per the JSON spec; Python's lenient parser tolerates them. The fix is parser-robustness, not parser-replacement: keep jq for the typed JSONPath ergonomics, strip control chars before parsing. | Pipe every Netlify API response through `tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037' \| jq …` before parsing. Range chosen to preserve `\t` (`\011`), `\n` (`\012`), and `\r` (`\015`) which jq tolerates; strip everything else in the C0 control range. Applied at 3 sites in S142's `deploy_to_netlify()`: deploy_id parse from `--json` stdout, state/error_message parse from `getSiteDeploy`, concurrent-count parse from `listSiteDeploys`. Pattern banked in `patterns.md` as the parser-robustness layer for any cloud-CLI integration. |
| **The S101a three-signal gate as originally framed conflated over-stating freshness with under-stating freshness, blocking deploys for the wrong reason.** S142's Part-A verification surfaced `<meta name="date" content="2026-05-17">` while visible `Τελευταία ενημέρωση: 18 Μαΐου 2026 στις 02:35 πμ` and `sitemap-events.xml lastmod: 2026-05-18`. Strict S101a interpretation says "three signals must agree, so this deploy fails verification." But the citability-penalty failure mode S101a was designed to prevent is *fraudulent freshness* — claiming content is newer than it is. A meta tag claiming the site is one UTC-day older than visible is conservative understatement, not overstatement, and AI engines weight visible + sitemap >> a single SEO meta tag. Blocking on this would have deferred the unsalt 5+ hours for no citability gain. | Gate strictness must match the failure mode the gate exists to prevent. S101a's "three signals align" rule was written symmetrically (any divergence blocks); the underlying citability principle is asymmetric (fraudulent freshness penalizes; conservative understatement doesn't). The symmetric rule is over-stringent against the asymmetric failure mode. | Adjusted S142 gate: visible-string + sitemap-lastmod REQUIRED to match today's Athens date; `<meta name="date">` divergence ACKNOWLEDGED non-blocking and queued as classification-(E). Pattern N in patterns.md formalizes the asymmetry. This was a user-side correction mid-session; planner's S101a rule needs revision before next freshness-gate session. |
| **Brief-vs-reality continued: deploy function was named `run_deploy()` not `deploy_to_netlify()`** as the plan and the gotcha note (mistakes.md:622+) consistently called it. The mismatch surfaced during Phase B.1's read step (`grep -n '^deploy_to_netlify\|^run_deploy' scripts/daily-automated.sh`). Brief-vs-reality tally for [[feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs]] increments by one. | Even on a tightly-scoped 1-file change, the brief's working name for the target function turned out to differ from the codebase's actual name. Cumulative tally: S71, S82, S95, S100b, S101a, S138, S140, S141, S136-revised, S142 = 10 documented sessions where Phase 1 verification caught a brief-vs-reality gap that would have wasted downstream time. | Phase 1 read of the actual function header (with `grep -n '^function_name'` or equivalent) before any rewrite remains highest-leverage. The 30-second cost of confirming the function name caught a Edit anchor mismatch that would have failed loud on first attempt. |
| **Diagnostic class ≠ proximate cause.** The Phase 1 diagnostic chain correctly identified the failure *class* — Classification (B), DEPLOYMENT phase erroring — and pointed at the May-14 S139-banked silent-rollback gotcha (mistakes.md:622+) as the likely shape. The plan was sized against that shape: verify state via API + retry-once gate. But the *actual proximate cause* of the recurring 04-10+ failures wasn't silent-rollback at all — it was a hard CLI failure (`Error while running build`) because `netlify deploy --prod --dir=dist` was running the configured build cmd without `--no-build`. The proximate cause surfaced only when the first manual deploy attempt (mid-execution Step A.2) returned exit 1 with that exact stderr — diagnostic-from-log-files alone couldn't see it because the script's `>> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1` redirected the CLI's own stderr away from `freshness-stderr.log` (which only saw the script's own `log_error` summary). | Reasoning from "the banked failure class" to "the implementation shape" is correct *for the class*. But mistakes in production often stack — the visible failure (state-stale prod) can be caused by the predicted class *and* a sibling class simultaneously. Sticking to "the diagnosis predicted X" closes the door on "what if Y is also true." S142's plan didn't ship `--no-build` — the executor added it during Step A.2 when reality forced the issue. If the executor had skipped the manual unsalt and gone straight to the script rewrite ("the plan said state-verify is the fix"), the rewrite would have shipped without `--no-build` and the next launchctl fire would have failed loudly with a misleading state=error error_message=⟨build failure⟩, requiring a second-session diagnose-and-fix. | Two-step diagnostic hygiene: (a) Phase 1 identifies the failure *class* from log evidence. (b) Phase A's first execution step — the first time real code runs against real infra — is the second diagnostic surface. Treat unexpected output at that boundary as a *re-diagnosis trigger*, not noise to retry past. S142 caught this because Step A.2 was scoped as "manual unsalt deploy" with real CLI invocation, exposing the proximate cause before the script rewrite locked in the wrong fix shape. Plans should preserve a real-execution diagnostic step *before* the rewrite, even when the failure class is "known." |

## S137 — Schema-emission grep-pattern miss (2026-05-19)

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| **Schema field emission grep matched only object-literal quote style, missed property-assignment style.** Initial Step 0b grep `grep -rn "'image'\|\"image\""` returned zero matches in `src/generators/event-page.ts`, leading to a tentative conclusion that `image` was not emitted on EDP JSON-LD. Step 1 live HTML probe contradicted this — the JSON-LD block had `image` present on every EDP. Broader re-grep `grep -rn "\.image\b\|schema\['image'\]\|schema\.image"` located the emission at `event-page.ts:229` as `schema.image = ogImage.startsWith('http') ? ogImage : ${BASE_URL}${ogImage}` — direct property-assignment style, no string-literal key, so the original grep missed it. Generalization of the "[[feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs]]" / "Enumerate by value shape, not just value source" rubric from S95: applies to schema field emission too. The same field can be added to a builder object via three idioms: (a) object-literal with quoted key (`'image': value`), (b) object-literal with bare key (`image: value`), (c) property-assignment after construction (`schema.image = value`). Grepping only for (a) leaves (b) and (c) invisible. | The same recurring class as S95's `T00:00:00` and "Enumerate by value shape, not just value source" pattern — the literal-string surface area of the artifact is not coextensive with the source-code surface area that produces it. The artifact (rendered JSON-LD `"image": "…"`) can be produced by several distinct source-code forms, and the diagnosis grep must cover all of them or risk a false-negative on emission. | When auditing whether a schema field is emitted, run **three orthogonal greps** against the suspected file(s): (1) `'fieldname'\|"fieldname"` for object-literal-with-quotes, (2) `\bfieldname:` for object-literal-bare-key, (3) `\.fieldname\b\|\['fieldname'\]` for property-assignment / dynamic-key access. Confirm by live-HTML probe of a representative URL — if the field appears in output but no source grep matches, expand the grep set before drawing conclusions. Live probe (Pattern B) is the ground-truth backstop; static grep is fast-path. Don't trust fast-path negative results without backstop confirmation. Named check: **"Three idioms grep + live probe for emission audit."** |

## S137 — `git log --since` timezone off-by-one when verifying recent ship (2026-05-19)

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| **`git log --since="YYYY-MM-DD"` is timezone-inclusive but hour-exclusive — late-evening +0300 commits on day D-1 fall outside `--since="D"`.** During S137 class-F probing, `git log --since="2026-05-19" -- <path>` returned zero commits and pointed at a tentative "nothing shipped recently" conclusion. Widening to `git log --since="2026-05-18" -- <path>` surfaced the relevant commit at a `+0300` timestamp late on D-1 Athens local time. `--since` interprets the date string as local-midnight (`2026-05-19T00:00:00` local), and a `2026-05-18T23:47:11+0300` commit normalizes to `2026-05-18T20:47:11Z` — before the local-midnight cutoff. The date string reads inclusive ("since today") but the comparison is on a timezone-anchored timestamp that excludes most of the prior calendar day's late hours. | Same failure-mode class as S95's `T00:00:00` mismatch: the human-meaningful surface ("since today") is not coextensive with the machine-evaluated surface (timestamp ≥ local-midnight). Athens at +0200/+0300 means the 21:00–23:59 window on D-1 sits >3h before the UTC anchor `--since="D"` will accept — a real "shipped yesterday evening" commit looks like "nothing shipped" under a naive query. This is dangerous for class-F (RESOLVED-IN-PRODUCTION-POST-CRAWL) assignment because zero `git log` results can be misread as evidence the field was never recently touched, supporting a wrong classification. | Always probe ship-verification with **`--since=D-1`** (or `--since="36 hours ago"`) rather than `--since="$(date +%F)"`. Treat a zero-result `--since="today"` query as ambiguous and re-run with the wider window before drawing conclusions. Named check: **"`git log --since` is hour-exclusive on D-1 — widen to D-1 for ship-verification."** Cross-reference: temporal sibling of S95's `T00:00:00` mismatch and the three-idioms grep miss above (mistakes.md:662) — all three are "the human-readable surface is not coextensive with the machine-evaluated surface." |

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| **Geocoder script name wrong + companion script missing from brief.** Brief referenced `scripts/geocode-venue.ts` (does not exist); actual canonicals are `scripts/geocode-missing-venues.ts` (Nominatim + Google batch) and `scripts/backfill-venue-geo.ts` (venues-master → events.db propagation). The propagation chain (geocode → venues-master.json → backfill → events.db) is a two-script sequence; treating it as single-script collapses the second hop, leading to a silent "geocoder ran clean but events.db unchanged" failure mode. | At brief-write time, `ls scripts/ \| grep -iE '<topic>'` to enumerate every script in the propagation chain, and read each script's header doc block to confirm what writes what. Brief embedded literal commands anyway. The deploy-memory document exists specifically to prevent this. Brief-author bypasses it whenever convenience > discipline. Each instance costs the executor one Phase 1 verification round to catch + one mid-flight brief edit to fix. | Brief checklist: when a step invokes the deploy CLI, reference `agent_athens_deploy_workflow.md` by name rather than embedding `netlify deploy ...` literally. Executor resolves to current canonical command at execution time. Treat a literal `netlify deploy` string in a brief as a Phase 1 catch surface — flag, replace with reference, ship. Each surface gets its own "what writes here, what reads here" line in the brief. Don't conflate the registry (config) with the source-of-truth (master json) with the cache (db). |
| **`config/athens-venues.json` carries `address` only — no `lat`/`lng` fields.** Brief Step 1b suggested updating `lat`/`lng` coordinates in this file. Coordinate writes to this file would have been silent no-op additions (jq would happily add the field; it would never be read by any downstream consumer because the schema-builder doesn't query it). | Schema inference from semantic adjacency: when a file has `neighborhood` (geo-flavored), the brief-author assumed `lat`/`lng` were also there. ## Session 1 Path D — Capsule injection wrong-anchor regex (2026-05-19)

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| **Wrong-anchor `html.replace` on `</header>` (a tag that appears multiple times in the document).** Capsule + category-nav were injected at body level instead of below page-header at TWO production sites: `src/generators/hub-page.ts:400-402` (capsule + nav for hubs) and `src/templates/category-page.ts:82` (nav-only for category pages). Both used `html.replace('</header>', \`</header>\n${content}\`)`. `renderPage` (`src/templates/page.ts:153-170`) unconditionally emits TWO `<header>` elements per page — `<header class="site-header">` (at body level via `renderSiteNav()`) AND `<header class="page-header">` (inside `.page-container`). `String.prototype.replace` with a plain-string anchor matches the **first** occurrence, which is the site-header's `</header>` at body level. Content landed between site-header and `.page-container`, ABOVE the page-header H1, inflating the chrome above the filter-bar by ~316px on iPhone SE and inverting the intended visual order. **Two of three Pattern R instances production-shipped before catch** — Pattern R was banked 2026-05-14 (QW-A test regex) but the production code that violated it pre-dated the pattern and wasn't audited until 2026-05-18. | Pattern R violation at scale: bare-tag anchors silently match the wrong occurrence when the tag appears multiple times. `renderPage`'s dual-header architecture (site-header outside, page-header inside) makes `</header>` ambiguous in any post-render replace — both sites had a load-bearing intent ("inject below page-header") that the regex didn't encode. The intent was carried in code-adjacent comments ("inject after `</header>`") which read as page-header to a human reader but as site-header to `String.prototype.replace`. **Comments do not constrain regex behavior; uniquely-identifying anchors do.** | Compose via `renderPage`'s new `preFilterBarHtml` 7th-parameter slot (Path D, Session 1 2026-05-19). Both fix sites now construct content above the `renderPage` call and pass it via the new slot, which emits between page-header `</header>` and `${filterBarHTML}` inside `.page-container`. Eliminates the post-render string-replace entirely. The new slot is the same compose pattern homepage already uses (`generate-site.ts:386-396` passes `homepagePreContent` via `preContentHtml`), generalized to the position hub pages need (before filter-bar). Cross-reference: [[patterns.md Pattern R]] (instance count now 3, mitigation refined) + [[patterns.md Pattern T]] (audit-self-disclosure rule class, new). One remaining Pattern R instance enumerated for follow-up: `src/generators/hub-page.ts:664` (overflow back nav, same `html.replace('</header>', …)` shape). |
| **Audit §5 claimed homepage emits capsule as "first child of `<main>`"; reality is homepage emits capsule via `preContentHtml`, which lands OUTSIDE `<main>`.** Plan-phase Explore agent + direct read of `src/generate-site.ts:386-396` and `src/templates/homepage.ts:55` showed `renderHomepageCapsule()` is concatenated into `homepagePreContent` and passed as `renderPage`'s 4th arg (`preContentHtml`), which `page.ts:174` emits between `${filterBarHTML}` and `<main id="main-content">` — outside `<main>`. Audit's "first child of `<main>`" framing read as a load-bearing reference pattern; if Session 1 had blindly mirrored it (e.g., "emit capsule inside `<main>` like homepage"), the implementation shape would have been wrong. | Audits can confidently misstate code state — even careful audits — when they describe intent rather than verified behavior. The audit's TL;DR was correct (capsule at wrong DOM position; fix via compose); its §5 "homepage reference" footnote drifted into prescribed shape rather than observed shape. Trusting cross-document reference patterns without re-verifying them at plan-write time is a sub-instance of [[feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs]] applied to audit-derived premises. | At plan-write time, always verify any audit's cross-document reference claims against the actual referenced code, especially when the audit prescribes "do it like X" as the fix shape. Cost: one Read tool call per claim; payoff: catching the wrong-reference-pattern class of error before it ships into the implementation plan. Session 1 caught this in plan-phase and surfaced it to the user via AskUserQuestion; the user chose the position deliberately (before filter-bar, outside `<main>`) rather than mirroring an incorrect reference. |
| **Slug collision between `config/categories.json` and `config/hub-pages.json` silently overwrites category output for shared slugs.** `generate-site.ts:508` runs `generateCategoryPages` writing to `dist/${slug}.html`. `generate-site.ts:535` runs `generateHubPages` **after**, also writing to `dist/${slug}.html`. For shared slugs like `concerts`, `theatre`, `exhibitions`, `cinema`, `comedy`, the hub output silently overwrites category output. Category content is generated, written to disk, then deleted on the next write — pure wasted work. Category output only ships for non-colliding slugs (`clubs`, `rebetiko`, `jazz`, `performances`, `screenings`, `workshops`, `tech`). Surfaced during Path D inspection when verifying whether category-page.ts:82 defect ships to production. | Two generators writing to the same URL space with no coordination layer — orchestration ordering masks the conflict. The architectural intent of having both category and hub generators is obscured: 7 of ~12 category configs produce overwritten (wasted) output, and the executor only sees the hub output. Not a Path D regression; pre-existing architectural smell. | Logged in `docs/known-issues.md` as 🟡 entry "Category and Hub Page Slug Collision — Silent Overwrite". Fix deferred — requires architectural decision on URL ownership (categories skip hub-shared slugs, hubs explicitly replace, or categories migrate to a different URL prefix). Not a demo blocker. **Cross-reference sanity-check (Step 11 grep):** searched `docs/`, `.claude/notes/`, `specs/` for `double.write\|generatePage.*hub\|silently overwrite` — **zero matches**. The "session 93 double-write pattern" the planner expected as a cross-reference does not exist anywhere in institutional memory. Either it was never logged, or it was logged under a search term I couldn't predict. Reported as a finding in the session report; the slug-collision entry stands alone without a cross-reference per user direction ("don't fabricate a reference"). |

## 2026-05-19 — S138 audit-first guard caught 3 brief-vs-reality drifts

The verify-assumptions guard in S138's Step 0 (audit current emission shape, 
emitter sites, validator topology) surfaced three planner-side claims that were 
incorrect on inspection. None landed in the spec as false premises. Pattern is 
working; these are filed as drift instances for cumulative tracking.

### Drift: Seller.@id-from-Sprint-1 framing

Brief framed Sprint 1 as having shipped seller.@id (used as the existing-
precedent for @id orphan-reference checks in Section 3b). Actual state per 
specs/s134-step-0-verifications.md:52 — seller.@id was deferred to Sprint 3, 
not shipped in Sprint 1. The seller field emits inline Organization shape 
without @id today.

Lesson: planner-side memory of "what Sprint N shipped" decays as sprints 
extend across multiple sessions with mid-flight scope changes. Cite spec/
session-log evidence for any "X is in production" claim in brief authoring, 
not memory.

### Drift: Homepage Organization emitter location

Brief said homepage Organization emission lives in generate-site.ts. Actual 
location: src/templates/page.ts:141. generate-site.ts orchestrates; the 
emitter is in the template module.

Lesson: file-location claims in briefs need grep verification before commit. 
The codebase's separation-of-concerns (orchestrator vs template) means 
emission logic frequently lives elsewhere than the orchestrator referenced 
in casual descriptions.

### Drift: Organizer emission state

Brief implied organizer was partially emitted somewhere in the codebase that 
the @graph migration would need to refactor. Actual state: organizer is 
never emitted anywhere. The Sprint 3 organizer work (S142) is a pure 
template gap fill, not a refactor.

Lesson: distinguish "field exists in some emitter and needs migration" from 
"field is absent entirely and needs new emission code." Brief authoring 
should grep for actual emission presence, not assume from validator 
references or session-log mentions.

## Diagnosing a defect from rendered appearance instead of source (4x this sprint)

**Sessions:** S105 arc (2026-05-14 → 2026-05-20)

Four times this sprint a defect or spec premise was diagnosed from rendered output (screenshot, audit snapshot taken at the wrong viewport, prior-doc claim) rather than the production source, and was wrong:

1. **Homepage compose pattern** (Path D recon, 2026-05-19). An earlier audit claimed the homepage's first-child-of-main was the capsule; production source showed `preContentHtml` was emitted **outside** `<main>` via a separate slot. The "first-child-of-main" framing was an output-shape inference that source disproved at recon.
2. **Category-page defect shape** (Path D, 2026-05-19). Asserted "same-as-hub" without inspection — turned out structurally same, but the assertion was unverified luck, not source-grounded reasoning. (A near-miss in this list, but the methodology was identical to instances 3 and 4.)
3. **595px capsule height** (2026-05-18). A measurement taken at a 199px-wide viewport (Chrome extension panel confound) entered Design Navigator's spec as if it were the 375px iPhone SE figure. Re-measurement at the true 375px yielded 316px — a 47% over-estimate that would have shipped if the executor hadn't re-measured at recon.
4. **Category-nav "circles"** (2026-05-20). Design Navigator diagnosed circular pills from a rendered screenshot; production source showed 20px-radius capsules already. Real bug was missing `flex: 0 0 auto` + `white-space: nowrap` (compression + wrap, not shape). DN also bundled an **unruled visual restyle** (transparent bg + 1px border + `aria-current="page"` migration) on top of the misdiagnosed bug fix — Dev Planner refused to ship it, routed it back to DN, who withdrew the restyle on re-ruling.

**Each was caught at executor recon, not at brief-write time.** Worst was #4 — the bundled restyle would have shipped a permanent design change to 2,400+ pages days before demo if the executor had treated the brief's diagnosis as authoritative. The verify-assumptions guard fired correctly each time, but always **late** — after the brief had already framed the work around the wrong premise. The recon round each time costs ~15-30 min and forces a clarification cycle with the briefing agent.

**Mitigation (uniform across all 4):** see `patterns.md` Pattern T's generalized grounding rule + structural mitigation. Practice change at brief-write time: briefs **establish** structural facts via recon instructions, not **assert** them. Any "the current code does X" sentence in a brief must be paired with a source citation (file:line) verified at brief-write, or rewritten as "locate the current shape of X and report." This moves the grounding from executor-recon (where it currently fires) to brief-write (where it can prevent the misframing entirely).

**Why grouped as one entry, not four:** they're four instances of the same rule-class mistake — diagnose-from-output-instead-of-source. Listing them separately would obscure the shared mechanism. Pattern T is the rule class; this entry is the cross-instance accounting that justifies the structural mitigation.

## Validator-coverage gap — in-build validator checks presence, not Schema.org vocabulary validity (4x this sprint)

**Sessions:** S137 (organizer) / S139 Stage 5 (@graph-flatten) / S139-fix-1 (nested-Offer-price) / S139-fix-2 (map-value-vocabulary). Cluster spans 2026-05-19 → 2026-05-20.

Four times this sprint a Schema.org defect shipped through a clean in-build validator and was caught externally (validator.schema.org or GSC export):

1. **S137 — organizer field gap.** EDP pages emit Event-shaped data through JSON-LD + microdata. The in-build validator checked `name`, `startDate`, `location.name`, etc. — but not `organizer` presence. GSC export flagged 256 instances. Two emission surfaces both lacked the field; the validator had no rule for it.
2. **S139 Stage 5 — @graph-flatten.** Pre-Stage-1 fix: `extractAllJsonLd` iterated all `<script>` blocks but did NOT unwrap `@graph` envelopes. When the only HTML block was the envelope (post-migration), the validator fell back to validating the envelope itself as an Event entity → cascade of "missing field" errors (4153 failures observed pre-fix). The validator's presence checks were structurally correct but it couldn't reach the entities. Fix: `flattenGraph()` + `resolveSamePageReferences()` at the validator's extraction boundary, absorbed into Stage 1 commit `32bac9a0c`.
3. **S139-fix-1 — nested-Offer-price.** validator.schema.org rejected 15 ListItem Offer instances with `priceCurrency` + `availability` but no `price`. The in-build emitted-Offer-shape rule covered event-page surface (top-level `Event.offers`) but never walked `CollectionPage.mainEntity.itemListElement[].item.offers`. Worse: the "price OR priceSpecification required" rule didn't exist anywhere — the existing rule validated price *format* if present, not price *presence*. Fix: extract `validateOfferShape` shared helper + extend `validateHubSchema` to walk ListItem tree + add the missing presence rule. Commit `7109ff809`.
4. **S139-fix-2 — VENUE_TYPE_MAP type vocabulary.** validator.schema.org rejected `ExhibitionCenter` (not a Schema.org type) on three production surfaces. The single-source-of-truth map at `quality-gates.ts:862` had a fabricated value; no test asserted map values against the Schema.org vocabulary. The other map values (`MusicVenue`, `PerformingArtsTheater`, `MovieTheater`) happened to be real, masking the gap. Fix: swap to `EventVenue` + vendored static allowlist test asserting every `VENUE_TYPE_MAP` value is a real Schema.org venue type. Commit `b5e875b47`.

### Meta-finding — the shared root

All four share **one** root: the in-build validator at `src/validators/schema-completeness.ts` (and its `validateMicrodata` sibling) was built as a **structural-presence checker** — does field X exist? is value Y a non-empty string? does block Z parse? It was never built as a Schema.org **vocabulary / property-validity checker** — is type X a real Schema.org type? does field Y belong on this entity? does this `@type` accept this property?

Both checks matter, but they catch different drift classes. Structural-presence catches "we forgot to emit field X." Vocabulary-validity catches "we emitted field X with a value Schema.org's parser will reject." The pattern this sprint: the structural-presence side was hardened progressively; the vocabulary-validity side was untouched. Every external-caught defect this sprint was a vocabulary-validity miss.

### Process invariant (elevated from session lesson)

**validator.schema.org as mandatory deploy-gate for any schema-affecting change is now a proven process invariant**, not a per-session decision. RRT remains useful for entity detection, GSC reports remain useful for production-corpus surveys, but validator.schema.org is the only external check that consistently catches the vocabulary-validity drift class that the in-build validator is structurally blind to. The constructive complement: each external-caught defect should be paired with an **internal** check — a new property-validity FAIL rule, a vocabulary allowlist, or a coverage-manifest entry — so the gap between in-build and external validation progressively closes. See `patterns.md` for the discipline rule.

### Why grouped as one entry, not four

The shared mechanism is the load-bearing institutional knowledge — listing each instance separately would obscure that they're all the same coverage-gap class. The meta-finding (presence vs vocabulary-validity) is what informs every future schema change: when adding a new schema field or type-mapping, ask "is the in-build validator structurally capable of catching the failure mode?" If the answer is "no" (the validator only checks presence, you're adding a vocabulary-validity question), the change requires a new internal check AND a validator.schema.org gate before deploy.

| Pivot-deferred items evaporate from tracking when held only by session-log narrative | Pre-S2a-impl plan-mode pivoted from "ship A+B+C" to "ship A only; B and C are safe halves, defer." The deferral was mentioned in plan-mode chatter but never landed as a durable artifact (no `known-issues.md` entry, no `specs/<topic>-deferred.md`). The session-log captured "we chose to ship A" but the chronicle isn't a tracker — items mentioned only there have no consumer who routinely checks them. Today's session rediscovered B (`.filter-bar-scroll` fade-mask) and C (category-nav `.active` → `aria-current`) only because a user-driven `grep` asked "did these ship?" — they hadn't, and ~24h of decoupled-but-coupled risk sat in the working tree silently (the inflight CSS-move of category-nav rules from inline `<style>` to central CSS was unstaged the whole time, vulnerable to being overwritten or re-done by a parallel session). Compare: the SAME session's filter-URL Clear gap WAS logged correctly in `known-issues.md` at deferral time, survived, can be picked up cleanly. Two deferrals, same session, opposite outcomes — the durable-artifact-at-deferral-time discipline is what distinguished them. | When a plan pivots, log the deferred change AT THE PIVOT MOMENT in `docs/known-issues.md` (severity tier + fix plan + cross-references) or `specs/<topic>-deferred.md` for multi-page scope. Do NOT rely on the session-log narrative — that's chronicle, not tracker, and has no consumer who scans it for "what's owed." Plan-mode chat is ephemeral. The check: "if we shipped this plan and a future session asked 'what's left here?', would the answer be findable via grep on `docs/` or `specs/`?" If not, the deferral needs a durable artifact before the session ends. See `patterns.md` → Pattern U for the constructive rule. |

### Validator-coverage-drift: resolution-function shape-assumption (discovered S141, 2026-05-20; root cause corrected S143 finish-forward, 2026-05-21)

**Symptom:** S143 working-tree WIP narrowed `Event.location` to `{@type, @id, name, address}` (geo + sameAs remain on the canonical MusicVenue @graph member per Strategist 2026-05-20, reached via @id merge). Result: 3815/3857 events flipped pass→warn at build time. Confirmed via stash-and-rebuild controlled experiment.

**Root cause (corrected 2026-05-21):** the validator's `schema.location.geo` check is reading the *correct* node — the resolved Event.location. The defect lives in the resolver. `resolveSamePageReferences` (`schema-completeness.ts:454-479`) only merges single-key bare-`@id` references (`if (keys.length === 1 && keys[0] === '@id')`). When the S143 emitter shape change made `Event.location` multi-key inline-with-@id (still carrying a same-page `@id`), the resolver silently no-oped the merge — the canonical venue node's `geo`/`sameAs` never flowed into `schema.location` post-resolution. The check then fired WARN universally because geo was genuinely absent from the inline projection. **The check was NOT inspecting the wrong node; the resolver's shape predicate broke when the emission shape evolved.** (Earlier framing — "checks pinned to the wrong node" — recorded inaccurately at S141 ledger time; corrected here. Mechanism matters because the fix surface differs: re-pointing checks vs. extending the resolver vs. scoping the surface — three different remediations, only the third is what shipped.)

**Class:** validator-coverage-drift — when an emitter shape changes, every helper that processes that shape silently no-ops if its predicate is shape-pinned. Here the shape pin lives in the resolution function, not the check site. Same family as the S139-fix-1/-2 literal-vs-graph blind spots — in-build validator's resolution semantics drift out of sync with emission.

**Fix (shipped in S143 commit `369dfe905`):** scope-the-surface — demote `location.geo` from WARN → INFO on the event-page validator. Per §2.4 v2, geo lives on the canonical venue node; `validateVenueSchema` is the load-bearing geo gate on the canonical surface. Event-page INFO acknowledges the @id-merge model: geo absence on the inline projection is not actionable on the event-page surface. Simpler than extending `resolveSamePageReferences` for multi-key shapes (which would broaden the resolver's contract); keeps the resolver narrow and the surface-responsibility split clean. Residual venue-data geo gaps still surface via the venue-page validator (where the warning is actionable).

**Superseded by `292e97aee` (GEO 2026-05-20):** the demote in `369dfe905` was a green-build stopgap. The proper GEO-spec-aligned fix is in `292e97aee` — `location.geo` check scopes to the canonical venue node via `@id` lookup (`rawFlatBlocks.find(b => b['@id'] === location['@id'])`), falling back to inline `location.geo` for legacy fully-inline forms. Demote hid the routing signal (3857 events → 4 WARN); lookup surfaces 25 actionable venue-data gaps → Component-B sameAs/geo backfill. The deployed behavior is the lookup, not the demote. "Green by demote ≠ green by scope" — the right green build surfaces the routable signal, not silences it.

**Lesson:** When a brief moves a property between @graph members, grep every validator check AND every resolution-function predicate that names that property's shape. A pass→warn flip on thousands of pages signals a resolution-function shape-assumption mismatch as often as a check-node mismatch — both produce the same surface symptom (universal WARN), but the fix surfaces differ. Diagnose by reading the resolver's `if`-conditions, not just the check sites.

**Saved memory:** feedback_deploy_gate_vs_warn_shift (validator-coverage-drift discovery pattern; mechanism recorded inaccurately at S141 ledger time, corrected here).

### S138 streetAddress — premise misframe (executor ledger, 2026-05-21)

**Premise (from prior brief):** "~126 URLs/location gap" — implied a hundreds-of-rows backfill scope on the streetAddress dimension.

**Reality:** 23 warns on the place layer of `build-completeness.json`; 16 rows patched by the migration script. Two orders of magnitude smaller than the premise.

**Class:** brief-vs-reality / vocabulary-misframe (executor ledger). Action was correct regardless (config + migration + DB upsert), but the scope framing was off — an executor reading "~126 URLs" might've over-engineered the migration (batching, idempotency hooks, progress reporting) when 16-row scope didn't require it.

**Lesson:** quantitative premises in briefs ("~N rows", "X% of pages", "thousands of events") need source-of-record reverification (DB query, `jq` on `build-completeness.json`, `git log -S 'string'`) before sizing the implementation. The reverification is cheap; the over-engineering it prevents is expensive.

### Thessaloniki filter gap — 3rd recurrence because the documented fix plan was never applied (2026-05-21)

**Recurrence:** WE Πολυχώρος (3 Thessaloniki events leaking as `verified_athens`) is the third instance of `docs/known-issues.md` "Thessaloniki Event Location Filter Gap" since Session 7. Each recurrence has a different venue name (Skiadareses → Eightball Club → WE Πολυχώρος); the class is identical.

**Why it recurred:** The Session 7 entry's documented Fix plan was: "Add Eightball Club and broader Thessaloniki venue patterns to rejected-locations.json." That fix was NEVER applied — Eightball Club is still not in `config/rejected-locations.json` at the time of writing. The `known-issues.md` entry had Status:Open plus a "subagent safety net is reliable" workaround note, which discouraged anyone from touching it for ~10+ sessions. When WE Πολυχώρος arrived from a new path (more.com via `athens-venues.json` whitelist with empty `address` field), the safety net assumption failed — this venue doesn't reach enrichment (it's deleted at filter time after being rejected, never enriched), so no subagent ever caught it. It rendered as a Thessaloniki event on agentathens.com for the entire pre-demo window.

**Root cause topology (the recurring class):**
1. New venue lands in `config/athens-venues.json` whitelist without verified address.
2. Scraper writes events with `venue_name = canonical_name`; `venue_address` often empty.
3. `src/quality/location-filter.ts` Step 1 blacklist greps title/venue_address/description for "Θεσσαλονίκη" / "Thessaloniki" — finds nothing in empty fields.
4. Step 2 whitelist matches the venue name → returns `verified_athens`.
5. Site renders it as Athens.

Both safety nets (city-string in event text + enrichment-time subagent rejection) fail when (a) event text doesn't mention the city and (b) the event never reaches enrichment.

**Class:** documented-fix-plan-decay. The `known-issues.md` "Fix plan" field is not a task tracker — nothing routinely scans it and routes work. Entries with Severity:🟢, Status:Open, and a stable workaround drift into "permanent paper cut" territory; the next recurrence catches the team flat-footed because the workaround framing implies "no action needed."

**Lesson:** when a `known-issues.md` Fix plan is small and concrete (single config file addition), promote it to a tracked task with an owner at the moment of documenting — don't trust future-self to grep `known-issues.md` for outstanding fixes. Recurring-class entries (Severity:🟢 + Status:Open + Frequency:Rare-but-recurring) need a re-evaluation trigger registered with a consumer: pre-demo checklist, quarterly grep, or hooks-based reminder. The opposite is documentation theater — writing the fix but never shipping it.

**Cross-reference:** `feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs.md` series (verify premises) is the executor-side discipline; this entry is the planner-side counterpart (verify outstanding `known-issues.md` fix-plans before each demo or release). Both are forms of "documentation-as-tracker fails when no one scans the documentation."

### Sitemap no-slash push shipped silently for unknown duration (S153, 2026-05-23)

**The bug.** `src/generators/event-page.ts:841` pushed `events/${slug}` (no trailing slash) into the URL list that becomes sitemap `<loc>` entries. `src/generators/venue-page.ts:362` did the same with `venues/${venue.slug}`. The on-disk layout for both is `dist/<events|venues>/<slug>/index.html` (directory) → Netlify serves at `/events/<slug>/` and `/venues/<slug>/` (slash) → declared sitemap form 301'd from no-slash to slash. **3146 event entries + 35 venue entries** were declared as 301-source URLs in production sitemaps for an unknown duration prior to S153.

**Class:** latent declared-vs-served drift, undetected because nothing validated parity at build time until S153's `dist-canonical-parity` invariant was wired in. Canonical-in-HTML for these pages was already slash-form (event-page.ts:437, venue-page.ts:201) — both eyeball checks and code review on those surfaces would pass. The sitemap inflow lived in a different file (the URL push at the bottom of the page generator, feeding `generatedUrls` aggregated at `generate-site.ts:598/669`) and was never scrutinized for form-parity. **The bug existed in a code path that recon-by-grep does not reach** unless someone greps for `urls.push` *across the codebase* with a sense of which forms should be slash vs no-slash — and nobody did, because nobody knew there was a class-wide problem until the invariant fired.

**Production impact.** Bing's URL Inspection rejects "canonical points at a redirect" — and a sitemap `<loc>` that returns 301 is the same shape of rejection. Pre-S153, Bing was being told via sitemap that essentially *every* event page and *every* venue page had a 301 source. The cornerstone-only investigation (`/en/this-weekend`) missed this entirely; the bug existed long before S153 and would have continued shipping indefinitely without the build-side invariant.

**Why it shipped silently:**
1. No unit test exercised the sitemap `<loc>` URL form against on-disk layout.
2. The canonical-in-HTML for events/venues was correct, so any *manual* check of an event page would look fine.
3. Sitemap `<loc>` is "infrastructure," not "content" — code review attention naturally goes to the latter.
4. Search engine feedback (Bing URL Inspection) only ever showed one URL at a time; nobody traced the rejection upstream to "this is class-wide."

**Class:** declared-vs-served drift on infrastructure-level emitters. Distinct from content/copy bugs because the emitter sits in a low-attention code path (URL aggregation for sitemap) and the failure mode (search engine rejection) lags by days and surfaces per-URL, not per-class.

**Lesson:** when fixing a URL-form bug, **write the build invariant first, then fix what it surfaces**. Recon enumerates emitters you can name; the invariant enumerates emitters that exist. The two diverge — and the diverge is exactly where the class-wide bug lives. The S153 brief scoped to "EN hub only" because Step 0 grep verified event/venue canonical was correct; the invariant added in Step 3 unmasked 3181 violations across surfaces Step 0 had implicitly cleared. The pattern: trust grep to find what you ask for, trust the walker to find what you didn't think to ask for.

**Cross-references:**
- `patterns.md` → 2026-05-23 "Infrastructure invariant unmasked sitewide defect — canonical-must-be-200" (the pattern this entry instances)
- `decisions.md` → 2026-05-23 "Per-URL declared-equals-served parity" (the rule that codifies the fix)
- Permanent mitigation: `src/utils/dist-canonical-parity.ts` invariant (Tier 1 build-fail). Any future regression of this class fails the build before deploy.

### Edit tool brittleness — multi-line old_string spanning Greek + escape sequences (S154, 2026-05-24)

| What | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Edit tool kept rejecting an old_string that visibly matched the file content, even after the tool reported "tried swapping \uXXXX escapes and their characters; neither form matched" | The old_string spanned three lines including `<kbd class="search-kbd">⌘K</kbd>` (literal escape in source TS, rendered to ⌘K at runtime) AND `aria-label="Μενού"` (Greek). Some subtle byte-level mismatch in the multi-line spec (likely whitespace or a character normalization the tool didn't try) prevented match. | Shrink the old_string to the smallest unique snippet around the insertion point. Two lines was too much; one line `</button>\n      <button class="hamburger-btn"` matched immediately. |

**Lesson:** when Edit reports a no-match despite the visible text appearing to match, *shrink before re-reading*. The tool's "tried swapping escape forms" hint is helpful but not exhaustive — Unicode normalization, line endings, or other invisible factors can still cause mismatches. Time wasted on 3 retry-Reads ≈ 5 minutes; the eventual fix was a one-line target.

**Class:** tool ergonomics around multi-byte / escape-sequence content. Bug is in the executor's mental model ("if I can read the bytes back, Edit can match them"), not in Edit itself.

**Cross-references:** none in code (this is a tooling note, not a code defect).

### HTML-entity decode at ingest was symptom-patched ≥1 prior session, never root-caused (S154, 2026-05-25)

**The bug class.** `athinorama.gr` (and historically `more.com`) ship venue names with undecoded HTML entities — `&#171;` (`«`), `&#187;` (`»`), `&#39;` (`'`), `&apos;`, `&amp;` — that flow through `scripts/scrape-all.ts` and land in `events.venue_name` as the entity-encoded string. The location filter (`src/quality/location-filter.ts`) compares against `config/athens-venues.json` and fails to match because `Νέο Θέατρο &#171;Κατερίνα...&#187;` ≠ the decoded canonical `Νέο Θέατρο «Κατερίνα...»`. Same Athens venue, different bytes, no match. Result: 99 events stayed in `location_status='unverified'` (hidden from the site) purely because of an encoding mismatch.

**The recurrence — what makes this a `mistakes.md` entry and not just a `fixed-it.md` note.** The whitelist at `config/athens-venues.json` *literally contained* the entity-encoded form: line 68, `"Κέντρο Πολιτισμού – Ίδρυμα &#171;Σταύρος Νιάρχος&#187;"`. Someone in a prior session noticed an entity-encoded venue failing to match, traced the failure to "the canonical form isn't a variation," and added the encoded form as a variation. **Symptom patch.** That fix worked for SNFCC specifically — but did nothing for the 99 other venues that arrived encoded with different roots, and the root cause (no decode at ingest) kept producing new encoded rows every scrape. The variations-list got an entity-encoded entry that's now dead code post-S154, but only because a SECOND session traced the same failure mode and decided to root-cause it. The first session had the fix in hand and stopped at the symptom.

**This is the documentation-health tripwire firing correctly.** The criterion from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s "After Every Session" section: "Update `mistakes.md` with bugs found" — the bug isn't "encoded variations broke matching" (that was the SYMPTOM that got patched); the bug is "the team's instinct on a class-wide encoding bug was to widen the variations list rather than ask why encoded forms reach the variations list at all." When you find yourself adding a `&#171;`-bearing string to a config file, you're inside a symptom-patch and the fix is upstream.

**Root cause (S154).** Decode HTML entities at `src/db/database.ts:197 upsertEvent` entry, before `isAthensEvent` runs. Single chokepoint covering all `scripts/scrape-all.ts` sources (more.com, athinorama.gr, clubber.gr, ticketservices.gr, halfnote.gr, residentadvisor, snfcc, onassis, benaki, megaron). Pure function `decodeEventFields` at `src/utils/decode-html-entities.ts` using `he.decode` (full HTML5 entity table). Idempotent — safe on every re-scrape, fixed point on already-decoded text.

**Why this took a second session to surface.** The first symptom-patch left no trace pointing at the root cause. The whitelist variation `"Κέντρο Πολιτισμού – Ίδρυμα &#171;Σταύρος Νιάρχος&#187;"` looks like a legitimate alt-spelling, not like evidence of a decode bug. A future executor reading the file sees a venue with many variations; they don't see "an upstream scraper isn't HTML-decoding." The symptom-patch obscured the cause. **Lesson:** when adding a config entry that contains HTML entities, URL-encoding, double-escaping, or any form of pre-decoded artifact, the addition is itself a smoke signal. Either fix it upstream, or leave a comment in the config explaining why the encoded form is the canonical form (and update `mistakes.md`). Don't silently fork the canonical-form definition between "the human-readable string" and "what the scraper sends."

**Honest done-criteria (per S154 brief constraint 2).** Decoding does NOT clear the 99 entity-encoded events automatically — only ~2 of them have decoded forms already (or now) in the whitelist (SNFCC via the new `(Φάρος)`-suffix variation added this session; Daddy's All Day Bar via a variation that already existed and matches the decoded apostrophe form). The other ~95 decoded forms are still genuinely unknown to the whitelist — they're in the ~970-event Fix B queue, deferred post-demo. The decode fix's real value is **future cleanliness** (no new entity-encoded rows ever again) + **correct matching going forward** (when Fix B adds the missing venues, their decoded forms will match) + **closing the recurrence**.

**Class:** documentation-health tripwire — config entries containing pre-decoded artifacts. Distinct from the prior `documented-fix-plan-decay` class (Thessaloniki filter gap entry) — that was "we wrote the fix plan and didn't ship it." This is "we shipped a fix and it was the wrong fix; the right fix was upstream."

**Cross-references:**
- `patterns.md` → 2026-05-25 "Decode at the chokepoint, not at every entry" (the pattern this entry instances)
- `config/athens-venues.json` line 68 — entity-encoded variation, now historically motivated dead code; do not remove without re-scraping the affected events (some existing DB rows still carry the encoded form until next scrape).
- `src/utils/decode-html-entities.ts` (the decoder), `src/db/database.ts:197 upsertEvent` (the wire-in)
- Deferred (per brief): existing-DB-row entity migration via re-scrape (post-demo).

### Nav locale-awareness — five reusable lessons (S155, 2026-05-25)

Task: make the shared nav chrome locale-aware so English pages stop rendering Greek labels/links. Brief assumed (a) the saved-events link was missing, (b) an inert language toggle existed to wire, (c) the hreflang counterpart URL was reusable. **All three premises were stale** — the toggle was removed a prior session (a test guards its absence), hreflang was globally dropped in S144, and the saved link already existed. The real defect was narrower: locale-threading gaps. Five lessons:

1. **Locale-threading gap (shotgun-surgery).** `renderSiteNav` was made locale-aware but its siblings `renderHamburgerMenu`/`renderSiteFooter` were not, and most call sites invoked all three bare (defaulting `'el'`). Result: English pages silently rendered Greek nav. **Fix pattern:** when a shared renderer gains a `locale` param, ALL sibling renderers AND ALL call sites must be updated the same session. Verify with `grep` → 0 bare calls.

2. **Built ≠ correct.** The saved-events link existed (assumed missing) — but was locale-broken (English pages linked to Greek `/saved/`). "The link is present" is not "the link is correct." Check the *target*, not just existence.

3. **Dead-but-inverted helper.** `src/utils/locale-url.ts` is fully-tested and canonically-named but encodes an abandoned English-first routing posture (English prefix-less, Greek `/el/`) — the inverse of production (Greek bare-root, English `/en/`). Its green tests assert the *inverted* behavior, giving false confidence. Using it would have emitted `/el/` 404s. **Trace imports, don't trust names** (it turned out import-dead — referenced only by its own test).

4. **Stale-artifact verification (3rd instance — recurrence).** Verified `/en/today/` as the EN home target against (a) the incremental `dist/` and (b) a green hreflang test fixture. Both encoded stale reality — `/en/today/` is no longer built. Only a clean `rm -rf dist && build` exposed it. **Verify user-facing targets against a clean rebuild, never incremental dist or test fixtures.** (Cousins: lesson 3 above; the canonical-must-be-200 class.)

5. **Date-conditional hubs are not valid nav targets.** `today`/`tomorrow` hubs only build when events fall on that date → they 404 on empty days. Never point evergreen nav (logo, persistent links) at them; point evergreen surfaces at evergreen hubs (`this-week`, categories). Now confirmed in a 2nd component (`cornerstone-links.ts` → known-issues).

**Cross-references:** `patterns.md` 2026-05-25 "Locale-threading reaches all siblings + call sites"; `decisions.md` 2026-05-25 "Nav locale routing"; `src/templates/site-chrome.ts` (the fix); `src/utils/locale-url.ts` (the inverted helper); `specs/en-nav-copy-checkpoint.md` + `specs/lang-toggle-checkpoint.md` (routed deferrals).

### "Locale-aware chrome" was not a complete set — filter-bar was the 4th surface, search-overlay the 5th (S156, 2026-05-25)

The S155 nav sweep grepped for `renderSiteNav`/`renderHamburgerMenu`/`renderSiteFooter` and declared "chrome is locale-aware." But **chrome = everything that renders on every hub**, and the sweep's grep only caught the obvious trio. Two more locale-unaware surfaces were rendering Greek on `/en/`:
1. **`filter-bar.ts`** (`renderFilterBar`) — hardcoded Greek labels (Τύπος/Τιμή/Ταξινόμηση/Ημερομηνία + actions + option labels). Fixed in S156 (labels only).
2. **`search-overlay.ts`** (`search-clear-btn` aria-label `Καθαρισμός`) — found while verifying S156; still Greek on `/en/`. Logged, not yet fixed.

**Lesson:** when making shared chrome locale-aware, enumerate ALL components injected into the page shell (nav, menu, footer, filter bar, search overlay, any banner) — don't grep for the function names you already know. The completeness check is "what renders on an `/en/` page that contains non-ASCII Greek?", verified against a built `/en/` page: `grep -oE '[Α-Ωα-ω]+' dist/en/<hub>/index.html` surfaces every leak regardless of which component emitted it.

**Cross-references:** `decisions.md` 2026-05-25 "Filter-bar locale (labels now, behavior deferred)"; `patterns.md` 2026-05-25 "Enumerate chrome surfaces by output, not by name"; `src/templates/filter-bar.ts` (S156 fix); `specs/filter-bar-locale-checkpoint.md` (deferred chip behavior + the 5th-surface note).

### 6th locale surface: hub heading / date-group / Related-Pages (S157, 2026-05-26)

Continuing the chrome-surface enumeration: S157 found the **hub heading layer** rendering Greek on `/en/`, three sub-surfaces:
1. **H1** — `page.ts` `<h1>${h1Override ?? title}</h1>` fell back to `buildPageTitle` (Greek-only; only `/en/this-weekend` had a slug-gated override). Fixed: `hub-page.ts` h1Override = `config.h1En ?? config.titleEn` for all `/en/` hubs (config already had `titleEn`).
2. **Date-group headers** — `formatGreekDateOnly` with no locale → Greek dates ("17 Απριλίου") on `/en/`. Fixed: `formatDateOnly(dateKey, 'en')` (already existed in `i18n-date.ts`).
3. **"Σχετικές Σελίδες"** — hardcoded. Fixed: `STRINGS.relatedPages`.

**The recurring tell:** each was a render path that *had* `locale` in scope (or one helper away) but never threaded it — `formatGreekDateOnly` instead of the locale-aware `formatDateOnly`, a hardcoded Greek string, a Greek-only title builder. The completeness check remains output-based: `grep -oE '[Α-Ωα-ω]{2,}' dist/en/<hub>/index.html | sort -u` surfaces every leak. **Still open after S157** (logged, same `grep`): Related-Pages *link labels/URLs* (Greek combo, deferred with the chip-combo work) and the search overlay (`Καθαρισμός`).

**Cross-references:** `decisions.md` 2026-05-26 "/en/ in-page filtering + heading localization"; `src/templates/page.ts`, `src/generators/hub-page.ts`, `config/hub-pages.json` (h1En); `specs/filter-bar-locale-checkpoint.md`.

## S158 — GSC/Bing remediation: tolerated-error shipping, symptom-patch pollution, false-0 grep (2026-05-26)

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| `location` classified as error but build was warning-only | `validateAllPages` (schema-completeness) classified missing `location`/`location.name` as an *error*, but `generate-site.ts:1222` ran it "warning-only, never blocks build" — so venue-less and empty-`streetAddress` event pages shipped (GSC "missing location" + "missing address in location"). The classification existed; the gate didn't. Onset traced to a deploy after 2026-05-13. | Wire the existing errors to a non-zero build exit (S158 2.1′ detail-scoped halt, mirroring the price-type-vocab `throw` precedent at `generate-site.ts:182-196`). A field "classified as error" is NOT the same as the build *failing* on it — verify the orchestrator's exit path, not just the validator's `errors.push`. |
| Whitelist symptom-patch pollution — now a **class**, not an incident | `config/athens-venues.json` carried auto-added junk canonical venues (empty `variations`, `"neighborhood":"Unknown"`, no `address`): the pipe string `ΚΥΤΤΑΡΟ LIVE\|ΠΟΛΛΑΠΛΟΙ ΧΩΡΟΙ` (fixed 1.2) and three `TBA -` placeholders (fixed 2.2). They falsely resolved garbage venue strings to `verified_athens`, masking the real venue and shipping broken `location` / empty `streetAddress`. Same family as the S7/S17/S138 address-empty-whitelist recurrences. | Remove pollution at source (config) + recover the real venue (split-on-pipe → whitelist match) or suppress the placeholder (config removal → `checkLocation` returns unverified → surgical DB `UPDATE`, never the destructive full `filter-athens-only` which deletes rejected). Root fix is the resolver/scraper, not whitelisting the symptom. **Whole-config audit filed in known-issues.md** (post-demo Pattern-G). |
| Phase-0 diagnostic grep returned a false `0` | `grep -rl '"streetAddress": ?""'` (no `-E`) treated `?` as a literal char → matched nothing → clean `0` trusted as "address-completeness has 0 backlog" for five plan revisions. Real backlog: 21 detail pages. | A diagnostic command is itself a premise (see `patterns.md` S158, ledger→10 Pattern-B). For a load-bearing `0`/empty, prove the pattern matches a known-positive first, or use the verified form `grep -rlE '"streetAddress":[[:space:]]*""'`. Show the command, not just the count, when a plan decision rides on it. |

## 2026-05-27 — config-fallback fix landed on detail but not the hub ListItem surface (S158 follow-on)

| Mistake | What Happened | Correct Approach |
|---------|---------------|------------------|

Same field, same venues, two surfaces, one fixed. | When a render/emit fix lands, enumerate **every** emission site for that entity (Event nodes: detail JSON-LD, hub ListItem JSON-LD, venue nested-ref — inventory in `gsc-bing-diagnostic.md` 0.2c) and apply parity — same discipline as "enumerate by value shape, not just value source." Fix: mirror the fallback at `schema-graph-builders.ts:57`. |

S101a-B) | `validateHubSchema` walked `itemListElement[].item.offers` but never inspected `item.location.address` — so the 237 empty hub `streetAddress` were invisible to the build (`build-completeness.json` fail:0 was *consistent*, not reassuring: the validator simply didn't look there). The detail validator checked `streetAddress` (~:382); the hub validator did not. | A validator covering surface A but not surface B silently blesses B's regressions. When a field is validated on one surface, add the equivalent check on every surface that emits it. Fix: hub-scoped `streetAddress` ERROR added to `validateHubSchema` (does NOT extend the detail-scoped build halt — node-keyed hub halt stays Session-2). See `patterns.md` 2026-05-27. |
