## 2026-05-27 — validator-scope-follows-emission-scope; diagnostic reuses the build's own resolver

**Validator scope must follow emission scope.** A field validated on one emission surface but emitted on several silently blesses the unvalidated surfaces. The "2.2" config-address `streetAddress` fallback + its validator check lived on the DETAIL surface (`event-page.ts:176`, validator ~:382) but the HUB ListItem builder (`schema-graph-builders.ts:57`) had neither — so 237 hub ListItems shipped `streetAddress:""` with `build-completeness.json` fail:0 (the hub validator never walked `item.location.address`). Rule: when adding a field rule, enumerate every emitter of that entity (Event nodes: detail JSON-LD + hub ListItem + venue nested-ref — inventory in `gsc-bing-diagnostic.md` 0.2c) and add the equivalent validator check per surface. Recurrence of the S101a-B "validator scope < emission scope" class.

**A reconciliation diagnostic should reuse the build's own resolution, not re-grep.** The throwaway `scripts/diagnose-missing-location.ts` imported `flattenGraph` + `resolveSamePageReferences` from the validator and replicated only the trivial extract regex — so its per-node location verdict matched shipped truth exactly (incl. `@graph` `@id` inlining). This caught what the prior `grep -rL '"location"'` (2026-05-25) missed: that grep tested location-*presence* (the string anywhere on the page), not per-node `streetAddress`-*completeness*, and didn't walk hub ListItems → it reported the hub surface clean while 237 ListItems had empty `streetAddress`. Re-verifying against the *current* `dist/` with the build's own resolver beat trusting three prior aggregate specs (their detail conclusion held; their hub blind spot did not).

**Hub-scoped validator ERROR ≠ build halt.** The new hub `streetAddress` guard surfaces in `build-completeness.json` but does NOT fail the build — the location halt (`generate-site.ts:1256-1282`) filters `isDetailPage` only; `hub:` slugs are excluded. Promoting it to a halt is the separate node-keyed Session-2 decision (interacts with the by-design venue-page nested-ref omissions). Detection closed now; halt-wiring deferred deliberately.

**Read-only diagnostics against a shared mutable `dist/` carry a freshness window.** A diagnostic verdict ("detail clean, build passes") is true only for the `dist/` snapshot it read. In a multi-actor setup (parallel sessions, launchd builds, background scrapes) another build can regenerate `dist/` seconds later and falsify it. This session's "detail-clean / deploy-safe" claim was overturned within minutes by a parallel actor's *halted* build (commit `936cbf0d9` genres-flood + a ~02:00 rebuild) that wrote every page to `dist/` **before** the location halt threw — so `dist/` looked populated but was a failed build (`build-completeness.json` fail:106), and a re-run of the same diagnostic flipped detail 0→24, hub 0→198 (all ΚΠΙΣΝ). Rule: a `dist/`-based verdict is stale the moment another build may have run — **re-verify at consumption time** (before quoting a count, before deploy), and prefer artifacts carrying their own provenance (the build's `build-completeness.json` timestamp + fail count, a commit/deploy id) over a remembered number. Note the asymmetry: pages are written *before* the end-of-build halt throws, so a populated `dist/` does NOT imply a *successful* build — check `build-completeness.json` fail, not just file presence. Extends the S158 "tree-state is an unverified premise" lesson from source-tree to build-output.

**Connects to:** `mistakes.md` 2026-05-27; `decisions.md` 2026-05-27 (esp. point 7, the cross-workstream collision); `src/utils/schema-graph-builders.ts:57`, `src/validators/schema-completeness.ts` (validateHubSchema), `specs/missing-location-diagnostic.md`.

## S159 — "present-in-DOM-but-clipped-by-ancestor": diagnose with hit-testing, not computed style (2026-05-26)

_(Recovered 2026-05-27 in S160 from `stash@{0}` — written during S159, stranded uncommitted before commit. Appended out of date-order to preserve the intervening 2026-05-27 entry's structure.)_

Two independent UI bugs (search results invisible; filter dropdown invisible) shared one symptom class: the element is in the DOM with its OWN computed style "visible" (`display:flex`/`block`, `opacity:1`, `visibility:visible`) yet renders at 0×0 or is painted-behind/clipped — because an **ancestor** hides it (`display:none` parent, `overflow`, `mask-image`, or a trapping stacking context). Element-level computed-style checks pass; the user sees nothing.

**Diagnostic ladder that actually works:** (1) `getBoundingClientRect()` — is the rendered box non-zero? (search items were 0×0 despite `display:flex`). (2) `document.elementsFromPoint(x,y)` — is the element in the paint stack at its own center, or is it absent (clipped) / behind something? (filter panel was `panelIndexInStack: -1` = clipped away). (3) live experiment — toggle the suspected ancestor property (`mask-image:none`) and re-hit-test; if it flips visible, you've isolated the clipper. Node-count and computed `display` are necessary but NOT sufficient — both bugs passed those checks while broken.

**Headless reproduction is the tool when manual DevTools isn't available.** Christos can't operate DevTools; a Puppeteer harness (system Chrome via `executablePath: '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/...'` since the bundled Chromium wasn't installed, a static server with **correct MIME** — ES-module `import()` needs `text/javascript`/`application/javascript`) reproduced both bugs, captured `console`/`pageerror`/`requestfailed`, and proved both fixes — all programmatically. Verified `bunx serve` returns correct MIME, ruling out a MIME false-lead, then drove against Christos's exact `bunx serve dist` for fidelity.

**Verify-the-premise (recurrence — same discipline as S158 false-0).** The brief's "single cascade, one root-cause fix restores all three" was refuted by static + runtime evidence: separate `<script>` tags can't cascade, and the three were independent (colophon unwired; filters & search separate clip bugs). Reporting the refutation — not hunting the assumed single bug — was the unlock; the proposed try/catch-IIFE isolation refactor was correctly dropped as a non-fix.

**Connects to:** `mistakes.md` 2026-05-26 (S159 — display:'' reverts to stylesheet; mask clips dropdown; DOM≠rendered); `decisions.md` 2026-05-26 (S159 — mask suppressed when panel open).

## S160 — A "pre-<urgent-fix>" stash strands everything in the tree, notes included (2026-05-27)

A stash taken to clear the tree for an urgent fix is a debt against **whatever is uncommitted at that moment** — not just code. In S160 the same `stash@{0}` stranded the S159 *code* (recovered + redeployed) AND the S159 *session-log + mistakes/patterns/decisions notes* (recovered here, days later) AND a `scroll-container-overscroll.test.ts` WIP. Notes are almost always uncommitted when you stash, so they strand together with the code that needs them — and a feature looks "never-built" at HEAD with no surviving explanation. Sharpens the stash-strand lesson from "code can get stranded" to "anything uncommitted gets stranded." The post-demo guard (pre-deploy `git stash list` warning in the daily pipeline) covers both; the discipline is: re-apply or commit a "pre-" stash the same session, never let it outlive its purpose. **Connects to:** `mistakes.md`/`decisions.md` S160; `docs/session-log.md` S159+S160; `known-issues.md` "broke together is NEVER a cascade" prior.

## S161 — A query path in a brief is an unverified premise (jq/SQL path-verification) (2026-05-27)

A `jq`/SQL/grep path written into a brief is exactly as much an unverified premise as a file path or a column name — and more dangerous, because **a query against a wrong path returns `null`/empty, which is indistinguishable from "the field is genuinely empty."** The S116 brief's Step 0a (`jq '.event_level, .place_level' data/build-completeness.json`) returned `null` — those keys don't exist; real coverage lives under `.fieldValidation`. An executor trusting the command would have read "geo coverage = null = empty gap" and walked straight into building the (already-closed) finder. Verify a brief's query paths against a real artifact before the brief ships, the same way file/column paths are grep-verified. Adds query paths to the path-verification ledger (file paths: S71/S82/S95/S100b/S101a/S135; query paths: S116). **Connects to:** `specs/geo-finder-S116.md §4`; user-memory `feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs`.

## S161 — Segment by type before concluding a field is a gap (2026-05-27)

A corpus-wide coverage percentage for an optional field is noise when the field is only meaningful for some event types. `endDate` is absent on ~100% of concerts/theater/dj_sets — and that's *correct* (they have no end date; validator treats it as additional/`warn`). It is load-bearing only for `exhibition` (Tier-1 keys exhibition lifecycle on `end_date`). A corpus-wide "endDate coverage is low" reading would have justified a finder for types that should never carry the field. Always `GROUP BY type` (and apply the Tier-1 exhibition-aware date filter) before deciding a field is an open gap, and ask per-type whether absence is a *defect* or an *expected omission*. **Connects to:** `specs/enddate-gap-S116.md §2-3`.

## S162 — Reject scraper artifacts at the save seam, not per-scraper (2026-05-27)

When over-broad scrapers capture site chrome (filter-UI strings, header/logo text) as events, fix it at the **shared save seam** — the single point all sources pass through — not in each scraper. Agent Athens' chokepoint is `shouldExcludeEvent` (`src/validators/scope-filter.ts`), called once per event in `scrape-all.ts:saveEvents` (`:1359`, `if (!inScope) continue`). S162 extended the existing S100 mechanism (config-driven, not new logic): `excludedTitlePatterns` (whitespace/case-normalized filter-UI substrings, title only) + `rejectTitleEqualsVenue` (exact normalized title===venue, the bare-venue artifact). One extension protects all 10 sources and every future scrape (infrastructure-beats-content). **Placement matters:** artifact rejects run *before* `allowedKeywordsOverride` (like the URL deny-list) so a content override keyword cannot resurrect an artifact. **Guard against the new bug class:** a too-broad reject silently drops real events — ship guard tests (legit short title; title that merely *contains* the venue; real exhibition title) alongside the reject. **Connects to:** `specs/onassis-ingestion-defects-S117.md`; reused S100 `event-scope.json` pattern.

## S164 — Precise selectors at the capture layer complement the save-seam reject (2026-05-27)

S162 fixed scraper garbage at the shared save seam (`shouldExcludeEvent`); S164 fixes it at the **capture layer** so the garbage is never scraped at all. The two are defense-in-depth, not redundant: precise selectors (`article.sm-col-28-18`, anchored on the repeated card and excluding the outer `article.bg-white` page-chrome wrapper that holds the filter-UI string + section headings) mean filter/bare-venue strings never become candidate events; the save-seam reject becomes belt-and-suspenders. The method that worked: **spike the real rendered HTML first** (`page.content()` → `tests/fixtures/onassis-whats-on.html`), classify selectors + date shapes from that fixture, write fixture-based tests, then implement. Extracting the parse logic out of Puppeteer's `page.evaluate` into a pure exported `parseOnassisEvents(html)` (cheerio) is what made it unit-testable — the `page.evaluate` version can only run in a live browser. **Connects to:** `mistakes.md`/`decisions.md` S164; `patterns.md` S162 (save-seam); `specs/onassis-rewrite-S164.md`.

## S164 — Category-bearing sources: map the page's own label, don't keyword-guess (2026-05-27)

When a listing exposes an explicit category label (Onassis `p.blue`: `Έκθεση`/`Κινηματογράφος`/`Μουσική`…), that label is the most authoritative type signal — map it (`scrape-megaron.ts:categoryToType` precedent) rather than feeding the title to the shared keyword categorizer. The shared categorizer's keyword config has **zero** Greek terms, so on these sources it falls back to `currentType` and re-introduces the mislabel that the rewrite is fixing. Pattern: `onassisCategoryToType(primaryLabel)` first; shared `categorizeEventSimple` only when the label is missing/unmapped (and the orchestrated path re-categorizes at `scrape-all.ts:1387` as a third net). Guard-6 reuse means "use the categorizer for sources WITHOUT an explicit label," not "always call the categorizer." **Connects to:** `scrape-megaron.ts:categoryToType`; `specs/onassis-rewrite-S164.md`.

## S165 — Gap-is-open gate catches the 3rd arc refutation; capture vs absence is in the data (2026-05-27)

Briefed an og:image capture finder for 174 missing-image concerts. The gap-is-open gate (run FIRST) refuted it: all 174 are `image_source='not_found'` — the existing `enrich-images.ts` finder already ran on every one. 5/5 spike of source pages = genuine absence (only footer logos, no poster). A capture finder closes ~0. **3rd refutation in the S161→S165 arc (geo S116/S161, endDate, now image-capture).** The reusable move: before building a finder, segment the target population by `image_source` (or the equivalent already-tried marker) — `not_found` ≠ untried. "Capture gap vs genuine absence" is usually already recorded in the data; read it before fetching.

Two more S165 patterns:
- **The brief's own quality floor would have backfired.** Captured athinorama images are 250×300 (short side < the 300px floor). A strip-to-null gate would have *deleted* the 118 events that had an image → coverage down. Rule: **upgrade-then-gate, never blanket-strip.**
- **Self-hosted optimized images inherit the source's ceiling.** `optimize-image.ts` uses `withoutEnlargement:true`, so a 250px source stays 250px regardless of `MAX_WIDTH`. The GEO surfaces (og/twitter/JSON-LD) read the self-hosted `image_local` webp, so upgrading them required re-download from the larger source, not just a config bump. Always check whether a surface reads the raw URL or a derived/self-hosted artifact before assuming a URL rewrite propagates. **Connects to:** `specs/image-finder-S165.md`; `upgradeWordPressThumbnail` (src/utils/image-extractor.ts); `feedback_gate_gap_is_open_before_how_to_close` (memory).

## Dual build paths diverge silently when validator and pre-filter share assumptions

**Session 2026-05-28→29 (drawdown + plist fix).** Raw `bun run build` and `scripts/daily-automated.sh` produce different validator results on the same `data/events.db`. The daily-automated path runs the Athens location filter first (line 173, S110f hard-stops; line 180 `bun run scripts/run-location-filter.ts`) — that update sets `location_status` and skips non-Athens events before the build's schema validator runs. Raw `bun run build` skips that pre-pass, so events that *would* be filtered reach the validator at `src/validators/schema-completeness.ts:382`, which checks `location.address.streetAddress` non-empty. The renderer at `src/generators/event-page.ts:176` applies a config fallback (`event.venue.address || findVenueConfig(event.venue.name)?.address || ''`); the validator doesn't mirror that fallback. Intersection: raw build flags 124 false-positives that the daily-automated path doesn't see.

**Two convergent assumptions, neither documented at the seam:** (a) the pre-filter assumes the build won't see filtered events; (b) the validator assumes upstream nodes always supply streetAddress. Each is locally correct; together they create a silent divergence between dev/debug builds (raw) and deploy builds (daily-automated).

**The reusable rule:** when a build step depends on a pre-filter, *either* gate the build step on pre-filter completion (refuse to run raw), *or* make the validator self-contained (mirror downstream fallbacks). Self-contained is preferred; gating creates "didn't realize I needed to run X first" surprises for new contributors and ad-hoc debugging sessions.

**Named check for future build-system changes:** "Does the validator see the same schema the renderer ships? Does every entry path produce the same pre-filter state, or only the canonical one?" If only the canonical one, document it loudly at the entry point of the non-canonical paths. **Connects to:** `specs/dual-build-path-divergence-2026-05-29.md` (Planner ticket); `feedback_validator_retirement_surfaces_dead_emission` (memory — same family of "validator and emitter co-evolve" lessons).

## S165 (refutation) — Substrate-classification gate; verify-the-premise recurrence #10 (2026-05-29)

Recurrence #10 in the verify-paths-in-briefs ledger (the brief asserted a current-state defect — empty `genre`/`about` arrays in `dist/` — that did not exist; `grep -rE '"(genre|about)":\s*(\[\]|"")' dist/` = 0, which is also the brief's own §4 success criterion). Planner-side pre-brief checklist did not catch it; Guard 1 (executor Step 0 read-only probe) did, for the **fourth consecutive session** (geo S116/S161, endDate, image-capture S165, now genre-emission S165). Mitigation update: planner-side checklist is no longer the primary mitigation. Briefs that assert a current-state defect of the form "X currently emits/produces/contains Y" require the execution-probe at **write-time** — same query the executor would run at Step 0 — before the brief ships, so the brief author sees the empty result instead of the executor finding it later. The checklist as written is not preventing recurrence; Guard 1 / Step 0 is. (Christos's note this session: "every brief that asserts a current-state defect requires the execution-probe at write-time, not just at execute-time.")

**New gate: substrate classification.** Before applying a ruling to scope a fix, classify which surface the ruling targets vs. which surface the named defect lives on. In S165 the GEO Strategist "omit beats empty" ruling addressed Schema.org JSON-LD emission; the brief's defects (`[]` in `Event.genres`, S164's `['visual-arts']`) lived on the *stored field* surface that feeds `/api/*.json` (a flat data feed, not Schema.org). The two never connect — nothing wires `Event.genres` into Event JSON-LD, so a fix against emission would close zero of the stored-field defects, and the stored-field defects are not what the ruling addressed. A 1-line check at Step 0: trace the named defect from symptom (e.g. `"genre":[]` in some output) to the code that would have to emit it — if the trace dead-ends without reaching the ruled surface, the brief is mis-substrated and needs re-scoping before any code touches.

**New gate: validator-mode classification.** Before proposing a rule for a validator, read its call site and confirm whether errors are advisory (WARN-only) or gating (`process.exit(1)`). Adding a FAIL rule to a warning-only validator emits a WARN line and exits 0 — the build does not break. The S165 brief's Step 1 narrative ("activation will fail build, Step 2 closes intentionally") was built on the assumption `schema-completeness.ts` was gating. It isn't (`generate-site.ts:1222`: "warning-only, never blocks build"). Sister-pattern to "Dual build paths diverge silently" (entry above): that one is "which entry point runs the validator"; this is "what does the validator do when it sees an error." Same family.

**Naming convention for refuted briefs (decided):** original S-number + `-refutation` suffix (e.g. `specs/genre-emission-gate-S165-refutation.md`). Numbers are not burned — burning creates index gaps that read as missing sessions; suffixes preserve the linear ledger and make refutations searchable as a class. Applies to spec file names and to notes-entry titles (disambiguate with topic when the S-number has been bound multiple times, e.g. `S165 (refutation, genre-emission-gate)`).

**Connects to:** `specs/genre-emission-gate-S165-refutation.md`; `specs/image-finder-S165.md` (prior S165 refutation); `decisions.md` / `mistakes.md` S165 (refutation); user-memory `feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs`, `feedback_gate_gap_is_open_before_how_to_close`; sister-pattern "Dual build paths diverge silently" above.

## S100b (GA4 leg) — Bun-native GA4 import: default gRPC runs in-process (2026-06-03)

**Reusable GA4-import runtime/transport.** `@google-analytics/data@6.1.0`'s `BetaAnalyticsDataClient` runs **inside Bun under its default gRPC transport** — no REST fallback needed, no Python edge, no subprocess. Scenario A (pure-Bun) won the Step-1 runtime gate on the first probe (property 525325167, service-account key at `~/.config/agentathens/gcp-kpi-reader.json` via `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`). The `protobufjs` postinstall stays **untrusted/blocked** and the client still works — gRPC under Bun does not need that codegen step. So the default `bun pm` security posture (block postinstalls) is compatible with this client; don't reflexively `bun pm trust`.

Field mapping confirmed against the live response (positional — request dimension/metric order must match read order): dimensions `date`(YYYYMMDD) / `sessionSource` / `landingPage`; metrics `sessions`(index 0) / `activeUsers`(index 1). GA4 reports ChatGPT referrals as `sessionSource = "chatgpt.com"` (confirmed, 27 sessions/28d); perplexity/copilot had no live traffic to confirm their exact host strings — hence the near-miss guard below.

**Near-miss guard pattern (instrument the unknown without importing it).** When an allow-list maps a small set of known host strings but the *exact* string for some members is unconfirmed, log dropped sources whose substring matches an engine name (`perplexity`/`copilot`/`gemini`/`claude`) to stderr as `UNMATCHED_AI_SOURCE=<value>` — surface the first real referral under an unexpected host instead of silently missing it, while still NOT importing an unconfirmed string. Fail-loud beats fail-silent for the one signal a table exists to catch.

**Window discipline:** query COMPLETE days only (`8daysAgo→1daysAgo`), never `…→today` — GA4's current day is partial and revises for ~48h, which would turn idempotent "latest wins" into "latest churns."

**Connects to:** `scripts/kpi-import-ga4.ts`; `decisions.md`/`mistakes.md` S100b; `feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs` (memory — B-pivot premise was stale).

## S102 (Session 170) — Alias-to-single-engine summing BEFORE a last-write-wins upsert (2026-06-03)

**Reusable trap.** When two source keys map to one canonical token (`chatgpt.com` + `chat.openai.com` → `chatgpt`), they collide on the storage grain. If the upsert is last-write-wins (`ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET x = excluded.x`), the second colliding row silently **overwrites** the first instead of adding to it → undercount. The fix is **in-memory aggregation on the grain before the upsert**, NOT SQL-side accumulation.

**Why not sum in SQL** (`SET sessions = sessions + excluded.sessions`): it would break idempotency — every re-import would add to the stored value, so running twice doubles it. The correct shape is: sum within the import batch (a `Map` keyed by the grain tuple), then upsert with plain last-write-wins. Re-imports overwrite with the same batch total → idempotent AND alias-correct. Single source per engine (the S101 state) hid this; the alias is what introduces the first same-grain collision.

**Diagnostic before widening any map to include an alias:** check whether the write path is last-write-wins or summing. If last-write-wins, an alias mapping is a latent undercount until you pre-sum. `kpi-import-ga4.ts:transformRows` is the reference implementation; the load-bearing test is the 5+3→8 single-row assertion.

**Connects to:** `scripts/kpi-import-ga4.ts`; `decisions.md`/`mistakes.md` S102; patterns.md S100b (Bun-native GA4 import).

## Session 172 — Module-local DOM typing for Puppeteer evaluate callbacks (2026-06-04)

**Reusable pattern: when scraper code needs DOM types but src/ must stay DOM-free.** This project compiles WITHOUT lib.dom deliberately — `document` not compiling in src/ is the tripwire enforcing the SSR Tier-1 rule (AI crawlers don't execute JS; data must be in HTML source). Puppeteer `page.evaluate()` callbacks DO legitimately touch `document` — but only at browser runtime. The fix that keeps both: `scripts/dom-eval-types.ts` exports minimal interfaces (`DomDocument`/`DomElement`/`DomAnchor` — only the surface the callbacks actually use), and each scraper module adds `declare const document: DomDocument` at top level. **Top-level `declare` in a module is file-local**, so src/ keeps erroring on `document`. Existing `as HTMLElement`/`as HTMLAnchorElement` casts are satisfied with module-local `type HTMLElement = DomElement` aliases — zero callback-body churn.

**Why NOT the two obvious alternatives (measured 2026-06-04):** (1) tsconfig `lib: ["DOM"]` removes the tripwire project-wide AND introduces 2 new errors — lib.dom's `ReadableStream` is not async-iterable, breaking `src/scraping/subprocess-runner.ts`'s `for await` over proc.stdout (bun-types' is). (2) Triple-slash `/// <reference lib="dom" />` is NOT file-scoped — TS applies referenced libs program-wide, same blast radius as (1).

**Two adjacent gotchas from the same session:** (a) `@ts-expect-error` rationale comments must not repeat the directive string on a preceding comment line — TS treats EVERY comment line containing it as a directive, and the one landing on a comment errors TS2578 "unused". Put the prose above, the directive as the single last line before the code. (b) Test determinism via `globalThis.fetch = mock(...)` + restore in `finally` (geocode.test.ts is the reference) — `processEventImage`'s 404 test hit real httpbin.org and flaked whenever the response beat the 5s bun-test timeout; the stubbed `Response(status:404)` exercises the same `!response.ok` path at 128ms, offline.

**Connects to:** `scripts/dom-eval-types.ts`; `src/utils/__tests__/geocode.test.ts` (fetch-mock reference); `decisions.md` "Portfolio claim-string policy" (this session unblocks the tests-claim); session-log Session 172.

## Session 173 — DB-as-address-verifier + dist-JSON-LD fail classification (2026-06-05)

**Pattern 1 — the events DB is an address verifier the web can't match.** Two research-agent skips (HOOD art space, Τεχνοχώρος Εργοτάξιον) resolved instantly from `SELECT DISTINCT venue_address, source FROM events WHERE venue_name = ?` — when athinorama.gr AND more.com rows agree on an address, that's two independent authoritative listings tied to *the venue actually hosting our events* (disambiguates same-name venues, e.g. Εργοτάξιον-Agios Dimitrios vs Technohoros-Acropoli gallery). Wave 2 generalized it: all 33 drift venues had DB addresses; 22 clean two-source values applied verbatim, no web round needed. Trust gradient: two-source clean > single-source clean > anything mangled (name-leaked-into-address, bare numbers, conflicting values → skip).

**Pattern 2 — classify schema fails from dist JSON-LD, not from the report.** `build-completeness.json` holds only aggregates (no per-event fail list; totals at `.events.totals`, NOT root `.totals` — the brief's jq was phantom). The real fail set: scan `dist/events/*/index.html` + `dist/en/events/` for `"streetAddress": ""` (note the space — emitted pretty-printed), parse the ld+json block, extract `location.name`, then classify each name with the live `findVenueConfig` import (a bun script). This reproduces exactly what the validator sees and survives report-format drift.

**Connects to:** `specs/streetaddress-backfill-S172.md`; `src/quality/location-filter.ts` (findVenueConfig); mistakes.md S172-streetaddress (toothless hard-stop).

**Pattern 3 — any list rendered under an "upcoming" heading must route through `classifyEventLifecycle`, and the surfaces come in EL/EN pairs.** `pageableEvents` ≠ upcoming events (it includes past-active ≤45d retention), so every consumer that renders a forward-looking list from it needs the lifecycle filter — bare `startDate >= today` is wrong for exhibitions (running shows have past start, future end_date). The EL event pages build related-events in `src/generators/event-page.ts` but the EN pages duplicate the same construction inline in `src/generate-site.ts` (~line 624) — when fixing one, grep for the sibling (`renderEventDetailPage` callers finds both). Shared helper: `selectRelatedEvents()`. Verification grep tip: assert on `datetime="YYYY-MM-DD"` attributes (year-exact, lexicographic-sortable), not Greek month names — "Απριλίου" matches April 2027 too.

## Sessions 174–176 — Ingest chokepoint guard; single-emitter + paired-validator; gate-from-one-constant (2026-06-05)

**Warn-not-block ingest guard at the DB chokepoint.** The right seam for "flag missing data at import" is `upsertEvent` (src/db/database.ts) — ALL scrapers + email ingest funnel through it (precedent: S154 entity-decode, isAthensEvent filter). Guard fires only when the emission cascade would actually bottom out (`!event.venue.address && !findVenueConfig(name)?.address`) — not on cosmetic emptiness a config fallback covers; noise trains operators to ignore guards. Dedup per venue per process; greppable prefix (`[address-guard]`) lands in pipeline logs for free. Load-bearing TDD assertion: the event STILL PERSISTS (completeness never blocks collection).

**Single-emitter + paired-validator closes a drift class permanently.** hreflang: one helper (`utils/hreflang.ts`) all surfaces route through, one gate constant, a validator (`checkUngatedHreflang`) reading the SAME constant that FAILs the build on any hand-rolled emission, and a hard-stop wiring errors to exit 1. Emitter makes drift structurally impossible at write time; validator makes it un-deployable at validate time; the constant means doc claims (llms.txt) and reactivation can't fork. Gate-open shape stays pinned via a test-only override so dormant logic can't rot.

**Tests that pin a regression must flip with the fix.** 3 hub tests asserted the ungated hreflang emission (encoding the S144 lagged surface as "correct"); the fix flips them to gate-closed parity and re-pins the gate-open shape at the helper level. When a test fails after a policy fix, ask "was this test pinning the bug?" before patching code.

**Connects to:** specs/scrape-guard-S174.md, specs/hreflang-sweep-S176.md; S110 paired-validator precedent; S144 4-surface invariant.

## S161 — Satori-as-oracle measurement + async-precompute bridge to sync renderers (2026-06-05)

**Reusable pattern A — measure layout from the renderer you'll ship with.** When auto-fitting text to a Satori SVG tile, don't approximate with font metrics — use Satori itself. Satori vectorizes text to `<path>` glyphs (no `<text>` nodes to grep), but the SVG `<mask>` rect's `height` attribute IS the rendered content height. `lineCount = round(maskHeight / (fontSize × lineHeight))` recovers the wrap result. This auto-aligns the autofit algorithm with the final render (same fonts, same layout, same wrap decisions) → no drift between "what we measured" and "what shipped." Connects to `src/utils/tile-autofit.ts`.

**Reusable pattern B — bridge async Satori to sync renderers via a precompute cache.** Card renderers (page.ts, card-variants.ts, event-page.ts) are sync and live deep in template trees that would cascade `await` through every page generator if made async. Instead: a module-level `Map<eventId, svg>` populated by a single async `precomputeEventTiles(events)` call at build entry (right after `pageableEvents` is filtered, before any render). Renderers do sync `getEventTile(id)` lookups. Mirrors the existing `generateEventOgImages(events)` batch in og-image.ts. Pattern generalizes to any "async generator output needed by sync renderer" surface — precompute keyed by a stable id, sync lookup at render. Connects to `specs/imageless-tile-S161.md`, `src/generators/event-tile.ts`.

**Closed-loop arc shape (design-surface decisions):** S124 ships imperfect-but-shippable Tier 1 fallback → S165 spec routes the contradiction to Design Navigator as observe-only → DN rules → S161 build executes. Each step is small and committed; the architectural divergence (gradient CSS vs Satori PNG) was named, scoped out of S165, and resolved in a dedicated session rather than forced inline. Reusable: route design contradictions explicitly, don't try to converge them inside a feature session.

**Connects to:** `specs/imageless-tile-S161.md`; `specs/image-finder-S165.md`; `decisions.md`/`mistakes.md` S161; sister-pattern S100b/S102 ("Bun-native runtime gate" — precompute pattern reused).

**Pattern 4 — derived-@type above EventType, with the backfill supplying the signal.** When Schema.org needs a subtype the EventType column can't express (ComedyEvent on rows that stay theater/other), don't re-type the column — layer a resolver (`resolveEventSchemaType`, src/utils/comedy-format.ts) above SCHEMA_TYPE_MAP at every derivation site and key it on STRUCTURED tokens only (a tag the backfill writes after a human-reviewed dry-run), never free-text (the corpus contained a literal "is not stand-up" negation and 63 Comedy-tagged plays). Two hard sub-rules: (1) loaders must parse signal columns BEFORE assigning @type or the resolver silently never fires (rowToEvent parse-before-assign + loader-level test); (2) close with the Guard-6 confirming grep `grep -rn 'SCHEMA_TYPE_MAP\[' src/` — it caught a 6th site (generateSchemaOrg) the probe missed. Downstream eligibility gates (performer) must key on the DERIVED type, not the column. Validator recognition lands in the same commit as emission (S101a-B).

**Pattern 5 — detector-precision dry-run as the Guard-2 shape for re-type/tag backfills.** The correction script owns a curated anchor set + same-title sibling expansion + an explicit EXCLUDE map with reasons, defaults to dry-run, prints per-row classification (named-headliner vs club-night decided WHICH rows get performer entries — rotating-lineup club nights get null registry entries: omit > wrong value), and the apply is gated on a human zero-false-positive review. Idempotency proof = re-run dry-run shows 100% skip.

## S178 — Staging-strand mitigation closed-loop (2026-06-05)

**Closed-loop arc shape (3 strikes → mitigation):** S164 (athinorama-image strand, S165 repaired) → S165→S174 (event-tile strand, S178/S161 repaired) → **S178 ships the pre-commit hook that catches the failure mode directly.** Three instances in four sessions established the pattern; the hook removes the recurrence vector entirely. **Recurrence count is now frozen at 3.** A 4th instance after this would mean the hook is broken, being bypassed, or someone disabled it — and the fix in that case is to investigate why, not to add yet another notes entry.

**Reusable pattern — simulate the post-commit state, don't trust the working tree.** When a check needs to know what HEAD will look like AFTER the commit, the working tree can lie (in our case, by having an unstaged file present that tsc happily resolves). The defense: `git stash push --keep-index --include-untracked` strips the WT to exactly what the commit will create. Trap-based cleanup pops the stash on every exit path. Generalizes to any pre-commit check that hits the filesystem — secret scanners that don't notice `.env` was unstaged, schema validators that don't notice the new migration file isn't staged, etc.

**Reusable trap — `git stash list --format='%s'` includes a `"On <branch>: "` prefix.** Marker matching needs substring (`grep -qF`), not exact-line (`grep -qFx`). Tests C+D caught this in TDD.

**Reusable design — install via a tracked installer rather than checking in `.git/hooks` (which can't be tracked).** `scripts/install-hooks.sh` is idempotent and makes the per-clone wiring a one-liner. No husky dep, no framework lock-in.

**Connects to:** `scripts/precommit-tsc.sh`; `decisions.md`/`mistakes.md`/`session-log.md` S178; `feedback_stage_precisely` (memory — 3-instance ledger now closed by this hook); sister-pattern S100b/S102 ("precompute pattern", S161 ("Satori-as-oracle").

## S180 — Resolver-derive + manifest-paired offline gate (2026-06-05)

**Reusable pattern — verified-derivation manifest.** When config values can only be verified ONLINE (QID label-vs-owner needs Wikidata), don't put network in the build. Instead: the resolver writes a verification manifest (`config/performer-qid-verification.json`) recording HOW each value was verified (method + anchor + matchCount + date); the build validator is a pure OFFLINE consistency check (every cache QID must have a matching record; pageprops records must have their anchor URL present in sameAs; label records must have matchCount=1). Hand-editing the cache without running the resolver trips the gate. Online drift (ownership, label-uniqueness) is re-checked by re-running the audit script — two layers, network only in the one that's run deliberately.

**Reusable trap — ownership is strict normalized equality, never containment.** enwiki redirects "Dimitri Vegas" → "Dimitri Vegas & Like Mike" (the duo); containment match accepts the wrong owner. Normalization handles the legitimate variance (diacritics incl. Greek tonos, &/+/"and", trailing "(band)" parentheticals, nickname quotes) so equality can stay strict. Same trap inverted: a promote-path check that includes the entity's labels in its candidate set re-verifies the evidence that selected the entity — title-only or nothing (Leon of Athens / "Damis d'Atenes").

**Reusable guard — label-derived entities need an occupation gate.** Exact label + uniqueness + P31 Q5 admits any unique same-named human (ancient diplomats). For humans found by label: declared P106 must intersect performer occupations; entities with NO P106 statement pass (Greek-artist Wikidata stubs are sparse — the uniqueness and exact-label gates still hold).

**Connects to:** S110 paired-validator pattern (hreflang S176); QID-provenance rule (decisions.md S179/S180); `scripts/lib/performer-qid-resolver.ts`, `src/validators/performer-qid-manifest.ts`.

**Two-layer validator for online-only facts (S180).** Facts verifiable only via network (QID ownership, label uniqueness) cannot gate a network-free build. Split: (1) offline build gate checks pure file consistency — cache and manifest must agree, manifest written only by resolver scripts; (2) online drift (ownership/uniqueness change) re-checked by deliberately re-running the audit script out-of-band. Distinct from the S110 paired-validator pattern (both sides of S110 run in-build); this is S110 adapted for facts that have no offline source of truth.

**Recurrence ledger note (S180):** verify-the-premise count unchanged. QID fabrications were an audit-caught data-integrity class, not a brief-premise failure.

## S103 (Session 181) — Shared-emitter + build-stats singleton; cross-surface number consistency (2026-06-05)

**Build-stats singleton for per-page chrome.** The colophon dialog rides every page via `site-chrome.ts → renderSiteNav` (22 call sites). Threading a `stats` arg to inject build-time figures = shotgun surgery (Guard 6). Instead: a module singleton in `src/templates/colophon-stats.ts` (`setColophonStats`/`getColophonStats`), set ONCE in generate-site before page generation; `renderColophonContent()` reads it. The emitter `renderColophonStats(stats)` stays a PURE function (testable). Precedent: `BUILD_STAMP` (site-chrome.ts:137, computed once at module load). Both surfaces call the same emitter+singleton → byte-identical markup (Guard-6 parity is structural, locked by test). N-agnostic so a held stat lands later without layout change.

**Cross-surface number consistency is a hard constraint, not a nicety.** When ≥2 public surfaces publish the same metric, they MUST share ONE source or an answer engine can cite contradictory numbers for the same site (citation poison). Here `/proof` and the colophon both show the live event count → the colophon sources it from the SAME `pageableEvents.length` /proof uses (verified identical 2,424=2,424 in dist/ AND on the live pages), NOT from `build-completeness.json` (which is the PREVIOUS build at render time — written line 1255, after pages at 1015). Named check before adding a stat already shown elsewhere: **grep the other surface, match the source variable, not just the number.**

**Derive the type from the data to lock drift at compile time.** The "10 sources" count needed a single source of truth. `scrape-all.ts` had a hand-written `type SourceId` union; lifting the ids into `src/config/active-source-ids.ts` and deriving `type SourceId = typeof ACTIVE_SOURCE_IDS[number]` means `SOURCES: Record<SourceId,…>` fails `tsc` if the registry and the count ever diverge — and the build imports a 3-line config, not scrape-all's puppeteer graph. Preferred over `export const N = Object.keys(SOURCES).length` (which forces the heavy import) and over a parallel config (which drifts).

**Connects to:** `src/templates/colophon-stats.ts`, `src/config/active-source-ids.ts`; `decisions.md` S103; proof-recon.md (P2 source-count, long unresolved).

## S176 (Session 182) — One signal drives membership + @type; config-flag post-filter on a shared engine (2026-06-09)

**Dormant ≠ correct.** A predicate that produces the right output today only because of a lifecycle accident (the offending row already aged out of the upcoming window) is still wrong — it re-selects the next matching row. /theatre kept stand-ups out only because the last theatre-typed stand-up had passed; the predicate keyed on `event_type`, not the stand-up format. Fix the predicate AND ship a tripwire in the same change, or the tripwire arms onto a surface that still leaks (a landmine).

**One signal drives membership, @type, and label.** When a derived signal already governs one surface (`isStandUpComedy` → `@type=ComedyEvent`), every parallel surface that should track the same distinction must read the SAME signal, not a coarser proxy. Re-keying /theatre+/comedy membership to `isStandUpComedy` (the @type driver) — not `event_type` — is what makes membership, @type, and (eventually) the badge agree. Reuse the detector; never reimplement the signal.

**Config-flag post-filter keeps a shared engine generic.** `getHubEvents` serves 19 hubs. Adding comedy logic as a hardcoded `slug==='theatre'` branch would be shotgun surgery waiting to spread. Instead: an opt-in `comedyFormat?: 'exclude'|'include'` on `HubConfig`, applied as a post-filter after the base `filter`; only the two hubs that opt in change, the engine stays generic. `'include'` unions (deduped by id) so the existing tag filter's scripted comedies are preserved.

**Exclude on the POSITIVE match, never on bare absence.** The /theatre exclusion gates on `isStandUpComedy(e) === true` (a positive structured-token match: title/tags/genres/venue allow-list), NOT on "lacks workPerformed" or "lacks a comedy tag". Bare-absence would sweep circus/variety/magic/drag out of /theatre. Locked by a test asserting a non-comedy non-scripted fixture STAYS, and verified live: "Η Καρυάτιδα!" (tag `comedy`, no stand-up token) retained in theatre membership; 39 stand-ups, 0 in theatre.

**A wrong slug spelling silently disables a whole validator scope.** `HUB_SLUGS` held `'theater'` while the real slug/file was `'theatre'` → `validateHubSchema` skipped the theatre hub for an unknown duration (the loop `continue`s on `!existsSync`). Symptom is invisible (fail:0, just nothing validated). When wiring a new per-page rule, first confirm the page is actually in the validator's walk (grep the slug list against the real dist filename).

**Connects to:** `src/generators/hub-page.ts` (getHubEvents), `src/utils/comedy-format.ts`, `src/validators/schema-completeness.ts` (THEATRE_ELIGIBLE_TYPES, HUB_SLUGS), `src/generate-site.ts` (S110 hard-stop); `specs/comedy-badge-shared-surface.md`, `specs/s176-category-surface-followup.md`; decisions.md S176.

## Compute the mechanical-vs-residual split with the REAL matcher before batching (S182)

When a brief says "fix the *mechanical* subset" of a list (string normalization, entity decode, dedup) before handing the rest to a human, **don't estimate the subset from the messy strings — compute it by running the actual production matcher over each item.** S182's brief assumed entity/variant venue strings were the blocker; the real split was computed read-only as:

```ts
import he from 'he';
import { findVenueConfig } from '../src/quality/location-filter';
const decodedMatch = findVenueConfig(he.decode(venueName)); // null ⇒ residual, not mechanical
```

Result: the "mechanical" subset was **empty (0/201)** — every unverified venue was *absent* from the whitelist, not malformed, because the matcher already normalizes+substring-matches. The lesson generalizes: a "fix the easy ones first" brief is only valid if the easy set is non-empty, and the only honest way to size it is the real resolver, not eyeballing the inputs. **Refuting the mechanical premise at the discovery step is a valid, complete session outcome** — it shrinks the human's job by re-segmenting (objective tags: city-token / entity / dup-cluster), even when zero items were auto-fixed.

**Collapse guard (carried from S172–S180 wrong-binding class):** when a normalization *would* match, also assert it maps to exactly ONE entry and not a different venue — a rule that promotes by matching the wrong entry is worse than leaving it unverified. (Moot in S182 at 0 matches, but the check belongs in the harness.)

**Connects to:** `src/quality/location-filter.ts` (`findVenueConfig`, `normalize`), `src/utils/decode-html-entities.ts`, `config/athens-venues.json` (`variations[]`); `specs/location-verification-residual-S182.md`; mistakes.md "Location / Venue Verification"; decisions.md S182.

## A folded-match rule is validated against the whole match-set's ambiguity, not just today's sample (S184)

S184 tried to ship the S182-proposed accent-fold. It was spike-gated and **refuted before any apply** — the refutation is the reusable lesson:

**1. A shared normalizer change is bidirectional — prove it, don't assume it.** Folding the single shared `normalize()` was framed as "reject-only hygiene," but `normalize()` also feeds `findVenueConfig` (whitelist) + neighborhood matching. The symmetric collapse check (re-run the matcher BOTH ways over real events, diff ALL transitions) caught **19 `unverified→verified_athens` promotions**, including a distinct-place substring-collapse (Epirus camp `Παραμυθιάς` → Gazi street `Παραμυθίας`). **Always diff every transition, not just the one you intended.** If reject-only is the mandate, fold only the reject-side helpers and leave the accept-side (whitelist/neighborhood) untouched — then re-spike, because precedence matters (blacklist fires before the whitelist in `checkLocation`, so accept-side protection that existed in the full-fold spike vanishes in the asymmetric one).

**2. The spike sees today; the rule lives forever — audit the match-set, not the sample.** The asymmetric (reject-only) fold passed the invariant cleanly (0 promotions, 0 Athens false-rejects, N=17) — yet was still refuted. A **same-name trap scan** of the reject set found `Ηράκλειο` (blacklist city) is also `Ηράκλειο Αττικής` (Athens municipality): folding bakes in `ΗΡΑΚΛΕΙΟ→reject`, which silently+irreversibly deletes a future Athens-suburb event. Today's matches happened to be Crete (right-by-accident — the exact failure class S172–S180 exists to kill). **A folded/fuzzy match rule applies to the FULL match-set forever; a spike only validates the items with events in today's batch.** Before shipping, audit the match-set for ambiguous members (here: Attica suburb names colliding with other-Greece places — Νέα Μάκρη, Μαραθώνας, Παλλήνη, Νέα Σμύρνη/Σμύρνη). Ambiguous members **hold for human triage**, never auto-act — especially when the action is destructive (archive+DELETE).

**3. A destructive auto-action needs a higher bar than a non-destructive one.** `filter-athens-only.ts` rejects by archiving + DELETING from `events`. Reversibility changes the calculus: a fuzzy promote (recoverable) tolerates more risk than a fuzzy delete (not). When the spike's mirror checks (collapse + same-name trap) both fire on a destructive path, the correct outcome is **report-only refutation** — the fold *implementation* (`normalizeGreek`) survives for a later audited design; only the blanket application is refused.

**Connects to:** `src/quality/location-filter.ts` (`normalize`, `checkLocation` Step-1 blacklist vs Step-2 whitelist precedence, `findVenueConfig`, `getBlacklistTerms`/`containsAny`), `src/utils/normalize-greek.ts` (`normalizeGreek`), `config/rejected-locations.json`; `specs/location-verification-residual-S182.md` §5; mistakes.md "Location / Venue Verification"; decisions.md "Location verification — D1 refuted (S184)".

## Output-keyed cross-artifact invariant — robots-meta sibling to the S175 hreflang sweep (Session 184)

When two emitted surfaces must agree (here: a page's **sitemap membership** and its **robots-meta**), the build-FAIL guard should key off the **emitted artifacts**, not off a re-derived class list. This is the robots-meta sibling of the S175 single-hreflang-emitter pattern: same "all surfaces move together" doctrine, applied to a *validator* instead of an emitter.

Three properties that make it robust:
1. **Cross-artifact pass, not per-page.** The biconditional needs the HTML robots tag + all 3 sitemaps + the en-twin set *in scope together*. `validateAllPages` is per-page-HTML-only and structurally can't see sitemaps — so this lives in its own pass (`src/validators/dormant-locale-noindex.ts`), mirroring `validateDistCanonicalParity`. The brief's requirement was the *behavior* (`process.exit(1)` hard-stop), not the file location.
2. **Runtime-keyed, NOT disk-keyed, for "liveness."** "Has an /en/ twin THIS build" = `en/<slug>/` present in a (freshly regenerated) **sitemap**, NOT `dist/en/<slug>/index.html` exists. Sitemaps are rebuilt from the live URL set every build; dist accumulates stale artifacts. The first armed build proved it: a hub that dropped below the ≥3-event threshold (`dance`) left a Jun-8 `dist/en/dance/` behind — disk-keying would have false-FAILed a correct build. **Named check: liveness comes from the regenerated manifest, not the file tree.**
3. **Catch BOTH drift directions.** Rule 1 (in any sitemap ⟹ NOT noindex) + Rule 2 (live twin ⟹ noindex ∧ sitemap-absent). The original Bing defect was dropped-but-indexable (Rule 2); the SAME invariant caught the inverse — `/saved/` was noindex-but-in-sitemap (Rule 1). A one-directional guard would have shipped the inverse defect.

It also makes a latent coupling build-enforced: noindex reads `!HREFLANG_GATE_OPEN` (inverse-on-flip), while the sitemap-drop doesn't read the gate yet — so flipping the gate without lifting the drop now build-FAILs (page indexable but sitemap-absent → Rule 2). The validator turns "reactivate every surface together" from a comment into a wall.

**Connects to:** `src/validators/dormant-locale-noindex.ts` (+ test), `src/generators/hub-page.ts`, `src/templates/content-page.ts`, `src/sitemap/generate-sitemaps.ts` (`BILINGUAL_CONTENT_SLUGS`), `src/utils/hreflang.ts` (`HREFLANG_GATE_OPEN`, S175 sibling); `specs/dormant-locale-robots-meta-checkpoint.md`; mistakes.md "SEO / Indexing"; decisions.md S184.

## A machine-generated defect corpus is uniform — diagnose the generator, then trust the uniformity (S186)

The 11,633 "Εως YYYY-MM-DD" descriptions came from ONE template literal (`scrape-all.ts:607`), so the Step-1 classification matrix collapsed to a single class: 100% exact-form, zero prose variants, zero invalid dates, zero end<start. Two reusable moves:

**1. Before designing a parser for "messy" data, check whether the data is actually machine-generated.** One `git grep` of the literal found the generator; the diagnostic then *confirmed* uniformity instead of discovering variety. The brief's prose-variant test cases were still written (defensive, trivial) but the migration design didn't need to carry prose-handling risk.

**2. Spike gates on uniform corpora are formalities you run anyway** — if the 20/20 sample is NOT clean on a machine-generated corpus, that itself is the finding (a second writer exists). 20/20 OK here confirmed single-writer provenance; the 14 more.com/megaron riders matched the same shape because they copied the same convention.

**Connects to:** `src/utils/run-end-token.ts`, `scripts/migrate-eos-end-date.ts`, mistakes.md "Scraping / Data Integrity (S186)", decisions.md S186, `specs/eos-backfill-residual.md`.

## S187 — External-tool claims about length/size: verify the unit before the value

**1. When an external tool (Bing, GSC, validators) flags a length/size threshold, the first probe question is "what unit does the tool count, and what unit does my probe count?"** Bytes vs characters inverted this session's classification (54 vs 202 pages under 100). The unit mismatch is invisible in the output — both probes print plausible numbers.

**2. "Fixed last month" and "still broken" can both be true on different template surfaces.** The 1.5b meta floor fully fixed `en/events/` (0 under 120) while `venues/` (no floor wired) and short-composite EL events (pad under-shoots) carry the same symptom. Classify external claims per-generator, not site-wide — a site-wide median ≥ 120 coexisted with a 77%-defective venue template.

**Connects to:** `specs/meta-description-length-S185.md`, `src/utils/meta-descriptions.ts` (padToFloor :99, venue generator :196), mistakes.md "SEO Measurement / Probe Methodology (S187)".

## S188 (brief S185/D5) — Intersection discipline + the four-state ambiguous-token rule

**1. Config-targeting briefs need the file in hand, never memory.** Of six Editorial ambiguous-token candidates (Ηράκλειο, Νίκαια, Καλλιθέα, Νέα Ιωνία, Παλλήνη, Μάκρη), only bare `Ηράκλειο` was actually in `config/rejected-locations.json`. The other five were hypothetical — no live landmine, nothing to defuse. The D5 intersection (candidate list ∩ actual config) collapsed the work to one token; without it, the session would have "defused" five entries that don't exist.

**2. Four-state ambiguous-token rule.** Classify each homonym token on two axes — *in the reject config?* × *live events matching it?* — and the action falls out:

| | In config | Absent |
|---|---|---|
| **Matches live rows** | Active misclassification — event-level triage BEFORE removal | Coverage gap — route venue/whitelist entries to Editorial (Καλλιθέα stadium: 2 events, 2 quote-variants, not whitelisted) |
| **Matches nothing** | Silent landmine — defuse now while it's cheap (bare Ηράκλειο: DB-wide match-set was 0) | Hypothetical — no config action; Editorial awareness only |

Bare Ηράκλειο sat in the cheapest cell: zero current matches meant removal had zero blast radius, provable with one read-only query pass.

**3. Disambiguation levers degrade in a fixed order: postal → region-token → venue-string.** Schema check killed the postal lever (no postal/region column; `venue_address` is blacklist input but empty on the whole affected corpus — ticketservices doesn't populate it). Region token Κρήτη had nothing to bite on for the same reason. The only lever that actually fires for tour-stop rows is the exact venue-string entry (Καφενείο Ο Σωκράτης Αμφισσα pattern) — copied verbatim from DB `venue_name` so normalization is symmetric.

**Connects to:** `specs/d5-iraklio-step0.md`, `config/rejected-locations.json` (3 S185 venue entries), mistakes.md "Location / Venue Verification" (S182 accent-asymmetry, S184 ambiguous-token rows), decisions.md S188.

## A semantics generalization is a Guard-6 sweep with a disposition table, not an edit (S189)

F2b changed ONE rule (effective end governs) but the rule had ~25 consumer sites across 4 grep families. What made it land clean: every file in the sweep was explicitly EDITED or CLEARED-WITH-REASON before any edit (the brief's "done when" required the table). Three sub-lessons:

**1. The cleared half of the table is as load-bearing as the edited half.** filters/search-index/ICS kept exhibition-only daily-presence semantics deliberately (theater runs play select days — listing them daily over-asserts; routed to Editorial). Without the written reason, the next session reads those sites as missed.

**2. Date-typed semantics changes wake dormant fixture data.** 16 "regressions" were stale 2025 endDates in fixtures that pre-F2b semantics ignored. Sweep fixtures for the newly load-bearing field before debugging the change.

**3. The dead-code finding rides the sweep.** `cleanupOldEvents` (a DELETE with the old exhibition-only COALESCE) has zero callers — flagged, not edited; a dead destructive path with stale semantics is a trap for whoever revives it.

**Connects to:** decisions.md S189, mistakes.md "Lifecycle / Schema semantics (S189)", `specs/f2b-residual.md`, A2 F2/F3/F4.

## S190 — scope-flag ≠ geo-ancestry; resolver-before-write; decoder-decides

**1. scope-flag ≠ geo-ancestry (standing schema rule).** `verified_athens` means "list this event"; it is NOT a claim that the venue sits inside Athens Municipality. The `containedInPlace` chain must be geographically honest independent of the scope flag. Today `schema-geo.ts:83` conflates them by hardcoding `Q1524` for every neighborhood — that's the D8 gap. A non-Athens neighborhood key cannot ship until the chain is per-key.

**2. Resolver-confirm QIDs before any geodata write.** The 3 Piraeus QIDs were confirmed via the performer resolver's `fetchEntity` (label + P31), NOT web search or hand-assertion. Caveat: `fetchEntity` exposes no P131, and there is NO geodata-specific resolver — the located-in ancestry hops still need a `Special:EntityData` fetch for D8. QID enters config only via resolver output, never generation.

**3. Decoder decides, don't predict.** Step 0.5 ran the scraper's actual decode path (`decodeEventFields`, not a parallel raw `he.decode`) over each Καλλιθέα variation. Only `&quot;` changed (`he.decode` is a no-op on guillemets `«»` and curly/straight quotes `‘’''`). The brief predicted two decoded twins; the decoder produced one. Add a decoded variation ONLY when the decoder output differs — let it decide.

**Connects to:** decisions.md S190, mistakes.md "Geo schema is Athens-only (S190)", `specs/d6-kastella-step0.md`.

## decisions.md write-discipline (D-recon learning)

Writes to decisions.md must: (1) confirm single-canonical log first; (2) read the existing entry format + D-number scheme; (3) match both; (4) verify number-uniqueness before appending; (5) never pin a QID/anchor the resolver hasn't adjudicated. Failures this prevents: the S190 orphan (headerless rows, colliding D8 number) and the Q1524/Q1224979 anchor confusion (stale-mount vs live-log disagreement asserted as settled).

**Connects to:** decisions.md D12 + re-homed S190 section, `specs/d6-kastella-step0.md`.

## Every health check and every gate must persist its failure reason (2026-06-28)

A check that emits only an exit code is undiagnosable by design. The auth pre-check (`auto-enrich.sh:325`, `echo ok | claude -p --output-format json >/dev/null 2>&1`) discarded stderr → the literal failure was never captured, so the enrichment fire stayed unexplained for weeks. This is the micro-version of the deploy drought running 20 days behind an ALERT log nobody reads: **signal discarded at the source.** Rule: every gate/health-check writes its failure reason to a durable, *delivered* place (a log that's read, or an active alert) — never `2>/dev/null` on the one line that tells you why it failed, never a passive marker file as the only record.

**Connects to:** mistakes.md "Armed build-gate silently froze deploys", `specs/enrichment-auth-diagnostic-brief.md`, the deadman-watchdog follow-up.

## Deadman watchdog: cause-agnostic active-delivery monitor (2026-06-29)

A drought-class monitor must have four properties, learned from 4 silent outages:
1. **Watches all failure families** — deploy freshness, enrich freshness, pipeline health in one classifier; a new cause surfaces as stale-outcome even if its mechanism is novel.
2. **Runs independently** — own launchd slot (`com.agentathens.deadman`, 6h, RunAtLoad), never depends on the pipeline slots it watches; fires even when they're dead/unloaded.
3. **Watches outcomes, not just precursors** — `MAX(enriched_at)` / deploy-success age are PRIMARY (the user-visible symptom); auth-precheck / launchd-exit are CORROBORATING. June's auth precursor degraded gradually while the outcome (no fresh enrichment) was the clean trigger.
4. **Pluggable health-source** — pipeline-health behind an adapter interface (launchd today → routine-status after cloud session) so the substrate swaps without touching the delivery arms.
Plus: **every alert delivered three ways** (notification + email + heartbeat row); email-send failure escalates the local channel rather than failing silent; one email path, no flaky fallback transport. Epoch-ms end to end to kill TZ-parse phantom alerts.

**Connects to:** mistakes.md "silent-drought class", decisions.md deadman alert-channel, `specs/june-drought-diagnostic-2026-06-28.md`, `specs/enrichment-auth-diagnostic-2026-06-28.md`.

## Integrity floor before overwrite; breach on degenerate state (2026-06-30)

**Generalize:** any backup/replicate/snapshot phase must assert its SOURCE is non-degenerate BEFORE it overwrites a known-good copy — and any monitor must treat a degenerate primary (missing/empty) as a FIRST-CLASS, highest-priority breach, never an inferred side-effect. Born from the 06-30 incident where a backup of an empty `events.db` (114 B dud) overwrote the day's slot and the prune counted it as a retained day. The deletion was unattributable; the *amplification* was ours, so the fix targets the amplification — which is why it defends against any future cause, known or not.

Three reusable floors (`scripts/backup-events-db.sh`, `src/watchdog/classifier.ts`):
1. **Integrity floor before write** — gate the write on `row-count > 0 AND integrity_check = ok`; refuse loud (exit 1, stderr), never silent-skip (silent exit 0 on degenerate state is the S90 bug class). Write to a temp slot, validate, then commit — so a refusal leaves the prior good copy untouched.
2. **Size floor vs prior** — refuse if the new artifact is anomalously smaller than the last good one (`new < prior × ratio`); catches truncation that still passes a structural check. Ratio configurable, 0 = off.
3. **Validity-aware retention** — prune evaluates artifact validity (size/row floor), not just mtime; a degenerate artifact is purged regardless of age and can never displace a good copy from the retention window.
4. **Monitor on degenerate primary** — "the DB is gone/empty" outranks every freshness breach (it's the precondition under them). Don't let it surface only as a low-priority consequence (e.g. enrich-null masked by STALE_DEPLOY). Add `DRY_RUN`/path-override env hooks so the monitor is verifiable against a degenerate fixture without firing real delivery.

**Tested:** `tests/backup-events-db.test.ts` (8) drives the shell script as a subprocess with `SOURCE_DB`/`BACKUP_DIR`/threshold overrides + a regression guard against the real preserved `data/events.db.empty-2026-06-30` dud; `tests/watchdog/deadman.test.ts` (+5) covers `DB_MISSING` priority.

**Connects to:** mistakes.md "S194 backup-amplifies-loss", `specs/db-loss-incident-2026-06-30.md`, the deadman pattern above.

## Validity-not-existence gate; one canonical health predicate per language (2026-06-30, S195)

The 06-30 daily ran the whole pipeline against a tableless `events.db` because the wrapper's
dependency check was existence-only (`[[ -f events.db ]]`) and `getDatabase()` opens
`{create:true}` — so a missing DB gets auto-materialised as an empty 114B file that PASSES `-f`.
Fix family (the 4th and last degeneracy surface; backup + deadman were the first two):

1. **Gate on validity, never existence.** `[[ -f db ]]` is meaningless for a file that something
   else can auto-create empty. The real predicate is `events readable AND COUNT(*)>0 AND
   integrity_check='ok'`. New: `scripts/assert-events-db-healthy.sh` (wrapper) + `assertEventsDbHealthy()`
   in `src/db/db-health.ts` (build entry, before the 13,606-image copy).

2. **One canonical predicate per language, cross-referenced** (Guard 6 across backup/deadman/build).
   True single-source is impossible — the assertion lives in both shell (wrapper + backup) and TS
   (build + deadman). So keep ONE shell copy and ONE TS copy, each header-linking the other; don't
   spawn a third divergent inline copy. We did NOT refactor the shipped/tested backup this session.

3. **The guard must not become the thing it guards against.** `assertEventsDbHealthy` opens its OWN
   read-only handle with `create:false` — never the `create:true` singleton — so checking for a
   missing DB can't manufacture the empty file. (Descoped the singleton split — ~20 callers + 50+
   scripts + bootstrap dependency on `create:true`; the guard's own no-create open closes the
   re-fire without it.)

**Tested:** `tests/db-health.test.ts` (in-memory + real-dud regression), `tests/assert-db-healthy.test.ts`
(shell subprocess, `SOURCE_DB` override + real-dud). Full suite 2870 pass / 0 fail, tsc clean.

**Connects to:** "Integrity floor before overwrite" pattern above, mistakes.md "WAL read-time trap"
+ "build-against-degenerate-DB", `specs/db-availability-build-2026-06-30.md`.

## Gate-failure class = run the emission resolver, not a config-only grep (2026-07-04)

The F2b streetAddress hard-stop failed on 1 event page (Christmas Theater). To size the *whole class* before fixing (so we don't fix one and rebuild into the next), the instinct is `jq` over `config/athens-venues.json` for entries missing `address` — that returned **~200 venues** and is wrong. The gate validates the **emitted** JSON-LD, and the render resolves streetAddress as a fallback chain:

```
streetAddress = event.venue.address (DB row)  ||  findVenueConfig(name)?.address (config)  ||  ''
```
(`src/generators/event-page.ts:178`; error raised in `src/validators/schema-completeness.ts:424`, only when `location.address` exists AND streetAddress is empty.)

So a page only errors when **both** the DB row and config resolve empty. The config-only grep over-counts massively because most of those ~200 venues carry their address on the DB `venue_address` column, not in config.

**The correct way to enumerate a gate-failure class: replicate the emission resolver, not one input to it.** I ran the real `findVenueConfig` (imported from `src/quality/location-filter.ts`) over every pageable row (`location_status IN ('verified_athens','pass_through')`) with an empty DB address, and kept only rows where config *also* resolved empty. True class = **3** venues (Christmas Theater, Underflow, Μπάγκειον), not 200. Only 1 built a failing page (the other two: one far-future beyond the build horizon, one past → no page emitted), but all 3 are one scrape/horizon-shift from re-blocking, so all 3 got backfilled.

**Reusable rule:** when a build gate fails, count the class by running the field's *resolution function* against the real data set, not by grepping a single upstream source. Over-counting from a config grep would have sent a "backfill 200 venues" brief when the actual gap was 3. Extends the "verify the premise against actual data" ledger to **gate-failure sizing**.

**Connects to:** MEMORY verify-the-premise ledger, `feedback_gate_gap_is_open_before_how_to_close.md` (segment by type before calling a field a gap), `specs/phase-0-reality-check.md`.

### GEO Ruling 2 (2026-07-04) — three patterns

- **recon-refuted-premise (14d-sweep misread):** the ruling's "orphan-sweep removes past-event dirs at ~14 days" was wrong. 14d = the just-passed→cooling (index→noindex) `JUST_PASSED_DAYS` boundary; 45d = `RETENTION_DAYS` (past-expired, page not generated). Deletion is non-deterministic w.r.t. age (lifecycle-gated non-regeneration + an env-gated sweep that's normally off), NOT a timed sweep. Read the boundary constants before trusting a prose premise.
- **enumeration-bound-by-band:** archive-410 emitted via `_redirects` is ceiling-bound (~10k Netlify rules) → bound to a trailing 45–90d band (aging past 90d IS the prune). Correct `resolveEffectiveEnd` keying gave 6,246 (not the spike's raw-COALESCE 3,068 — multi-day runs ended-in-band but started-out-of-band). Force-410 (`410!`) defeats lingering-dist-dir shadowing.
- **build-time-manifest + fail-open edge (Deploy-B confirmed viable):** edge functions DO deploy under `netlify deploy --no-build --dir=dist` (probe: `/__edge-probe` → 200, `x-edge-probe: deployed`, quarantine clean). The both-locale unbounded 410 closure = a build-time classifier-derived slug manifest + a path-scoped fail-open edge function that Set-checks it. Recon: `specs/edge-function-410-step0.md`.

- **F12-pills root cause (spec guess wrong):** the mobile "( )" glyphs around filter pills are NOT a pseudo-element/font artifact — `.filter-bar{height:52px;padding:16px 0}` leaves a 20px content box while `(pointer:coarse)` forces pills to `min-height:44px`; the pills' overflow-x scroll wrapper clips them vertically, leaving only the rounded side borders. Fix = `height:auto;min-height:52px`. Lesson: reproduce a visual artifact in an isolated page and read the *box math* before theorizing about fonts.
- **step-function-vs-clamp unsatisfiability:** a "pin endpoints exactly + render identical at every breakpoint anchor" gate can NEVER pass for a fluid `clamp()` replacing a stepped media-query scale — the discontinuity (40→64px across 767/768) admits no continuous ramp. Check the SHAPE of the current scale before accepting a pin gate; also grep who CONSUMES a token before fluidizing it (`--type-hero`'s only consumer: `.error-code`).
- **prototype-by-transforming-production:** for redesign prototypes, surgically transform copies of real dist pages (script in `prototypes/redesign-v2/build-prototypes.ts`) instead of hand-mocking — SSR/GATE-2 properties and visual fidelity are inherited, real content prevents fabrication, and the transforms themselves surface latent CSS interactions (orphan-rule × grid compounding, capsule margin hole, duplicate Satori SVG ids).

### Satori text = plain string, not an XML sink (2026-07-05, F4)
Satori's object API (`children: string`) vectorizes glyphs and does NOT XML-decode its input — so text must be the FINAL human-readable string (decode DB entities, do NOT XML-escape). XML-escaping (escapeForSatori) is correct only for raw-SVG-STRING sinks like og-image.ts template literals, NOT for the tile's object tree. Verify Satori output by rendering a real trigger case to PNG (glyphs are <path>, not string-inspectable). F12 companion: coarse-pointer (44px) tap targets clipped by a padded content box — check the box math (height − padding, border-box) against the min tap-target, not "font artifacts".

- **One fold primitive per matching domain (dedup arc, S197):** accent-mismatch bugs are a CLASS, not instances — any two consumers that fold text differently (Latin-only strip vs none vs full) will silently disagree. When fixing a fold bug, grep for every parallel fold implementation (`normalize('NFD')`, `toLowerCase()` + compare) in the same matching domain and route them through one primitive (`src/utils/normalize-key.ts` `normalize()`). S182 (location) + S197 (dedup titles) were the same defect twice.
- **Marking-instead-of-deleting must defang every pre-existing DELETE path in the domain (S197):** `merged_into` tombstones are only reversible until the next cron: `remove-duplicates.ts` and `merge-duplicates.ts` still DELETE and would have re-detected survivor↔loser pairs the next morning and deleted the marked losers. Shipping the mark column REQUIRES `merged_into IS NULL` in every dedup eligibility/DELETE query in the same commit. Reversibility is a property of the whole write surface, not of the marking script.
- **Digit-token veto for fuzzy title matching (S197):** edit-distance tolerance and high token overlap both false-merge sequels ("Κωμωδία της Γειτονιάς 2" vs "3" = 100% significant-token overlap; "(2007)" vs "(1982)" film reruns). Before any fuzzy layer runs, compare the digit-bearing token sets — both non-empty and unequal → hard veto. Fuzzy equality additionally requires ≥5 chars and digit-free on both sides.

- **Phase-0 recon-with-override-authority = executor-side premise validation (S198):** a brief that opens with "enumerate the behavior owners; findings override this brief; STOP if a third surfaces" turns the recurring brief-premise error (#10/#11: owners/reachability asserted from memory) into a caught-before-write event instead of a shipped bug. S198 proved it: the brief's "exactly two delete-based dedup owners" was wrong, the Step-0 grep found two more, and the gate fired before any mutation. Bake a behavior-owner enumeration step into any brief that asserts "the N places that do X" — especially for delete/merge/dedup paths.
- **Behavior-owner REACHABILITY, not just existence (S198):** existence of a delete path ≠ it's reachable from the risk vector you're worried about. S198's "live daily compounding-delete" urgency was stale because the live cron only reaches the two already-guarded scripts; the real exposure was a human running the `status.sh`-recommended `clean-database.ts`. When triaging risk, grep who INVOKES the owner (launchd plists → `.sh` → script), don't stop at "the script contains a DELETE."
- **Scope a guard by the behavior, not the shared token (S198):** `grep "location_status IN"` spans enrichment-selection, price/ticket/geo/image acquisition, schema-gen, and health COUNTs — one token, many behaviors. Patching all matches would touch reporting and risk still-emitting loser pages. Identify the behavior you're changing (here: enrichment SELECTION = the `needs_enrichment` queue owners) and guard only those owners; verify each is live (imported by a real caller) so you're not term-chasing dead code.
- **A column guard is a fixture contract (S198, 3rd instance this arc):** adding `AND <col> IS NULL` to a query silently requires `<col>` in every test fixture that hits it. schema.sql is base-only here (migration-added columns absent), and several tests build their own minimal `events` table — so the guard crashed 13 tests. When guarding on a column, grep for every inline `CREATE TABLE events` in tests and add the column too.

### Asserted-file-exists can fail as UNCOMMITTED, not drifted (2026-07-05, S199)
The design-system.md corrective-sweep brief targeted `docs/design-system.md` with exact line anchors (L321/807/1893/1950/2224). The file existed **nowhere** — repo, git history, Obsidian vault, or `/Users/chrism` (depth 6) — yet `.claude/notes/decisions.md:4823` cited `docs/design-system.md §4` as canonical and a prior ruling had shipped a bug reading that §4. Root cause: the canonical spec lived only in a chat canvas / `~/Downloads/design-system.md`, never committed. The brief's line numbers were **VALID against that uncommitted copy** — once materialized into `docs/`, Step 0b matched exactly (4 focus hits at the cited lines, 182 tables intact). **New verify-the-premise sub-class:** a "the file at X says Y" premise can fail because the file is real-but-unmaterialized, not because it drifted.

- **Rule:** when a brief targets a file absent from the repo, before declaring the brief dead — (a) search `~/Downloads` / vault / canvas exports, and (b) check whether the decisions log already treats it as canonical. A doc-debt reference to a non-existent path is itself the tell that the file was authored but never committed.
- **Materialize from the clean source, never a lossy chat paste** — markdown tables flatten to `TokenValueUsage--bg-primary#0d0d0d…` and would seed the canonical spec with column-shifted hex/spacing values that Claude Code then builds from.
- **Corollary (Step 5 = 0 edits):** the "D1–D11 / 2,970-line stylesheet" framing was already reconciled before the brief was written — `redesign-spec-v2.md:24` IS premise-correction #1; residual "2,970" hits are factual line-counts (≈2,994 actual), and `known-issues.md:814` "D1-D11" is design-session labels (institutional-memory, protected). All 4 framing hits correctly skipped.

**Connects to:** MEMORY verify-the-premise ledger, `feedback_verify_paths_in_briefs.md`, `decisions.md:4823` doc-debt (now reconcilable against the committed file).

### Normalize the pointer graph BEFORE gating on it (2026-07-07, dedup-301 hardening)
A build gate whose invariant quantifies over redirect targets ("every 301 target emits a page") is only sound over the *condensation* of the loser→survivor graph — chains collapsed to terminals, cycles quarantined — never over raw edges. The edge-writer (daily marker) guarantees only per-run local consistency; across runs, marks flip and interleave. Consuming raw edges turned one corrupt pair into a site-wide freshness freeze (Jul 6). General form: when automation A writes pointers incrementally and automation B enforces a global invariant over them, B must canonicalize (resolve + partition unresolvable) before enforcing, and the unresolvable partition needs an explicit disposition (here: per-group fail-open + loud warn, freeze reserved for ruling-ordained cases). Fail-open beats freeze when the invariant can be preserved vacuously (emit NO redirect for the corrupt group ≠ emit a wrong redirect).

## Reconcile colliding gates by fixing data, never by weakening a gate (2026-07-07, Session 201)
The dedup-301 gate (no 301 to a non-emitting target) and the A0 hard-stop composed into a deterministic build freeze: survivor election never consults emission-visibility. The unfreeze re-pointed `merged_into` (reversible UPDATEs, swap survivor/loser) so BOTH gates stayed fail-closed. Pattern: when two correct guards deadlock, the bug is in the DATA or in an upstream policy (election), not in either guard — weakening a guard converts a loud freeze into a silent defect.

## SQL predicates mirroring TS logic must be GENERATED from the same source + parity-tested (2026-07-07)
`src/db/effective-end-sql.ts` builds the "is this event current" CASE expression from `config/lifecycle-presumption.json` via the same accessors the TS resolver uses, and `tests/effective-end-guard.test.ts` proves SQL ≡ `resolveEffectiveEnd` over an event-shape matrix. Hand-copying the rule produced 3 drift waves over 4 months. Companion seam guard (S95 no-bypass shape) fails the suite on NEW raw `start_date >= date('now')` predicates; allowlist is self-pruning (a migrated file still listed fails the test).

## Watchdog extension pattern: adapter → optional pure-classifier input → priority slot (2026-07-07)
New deadman signals (SOURCE_DEAD, ADDRESSLESS_VENUES, buildFailureCause, dbBusy) are OPTIONAL DeadmanInputs fields with defaults, computed by fault-isolated adapters (`safe()`), classified purely, and slotted into an explicit priority order. Zero risk to existing behavior (all existing tests unchanged), exhaustively unit-testable, and the delivery layers are untouched. Add future signals the same way — never inline I/O into the classifier.

## Deploy verification: platform state is the ONLY truth (re-confirmed 2026-07-07)
First manual deploy exited 0 through a pipe while the platform recorded state=error (422 at finalize). `netlify api getSiteDeploy` state=ready is the done-condition; a live curl of a changed URL is the belt-and-braces check.
